results.value: [REVISED in Q14: see the Q14 CH3OH entries; the Trot~9 K constraint, the chi2=53/6 Q-branch excess and the Band-5 blend integral of this entry are baseline-limited (blend integral 0.9-1.9 K km/s over L/Q/R baselines; p0001 value = linear-baseline end), not established.] Q J=1-3: 1.71+-0.06 K km/s; 2(0)-1(-1) E: Xb4f 0.263+-0.028, Xb4d 0.146+-0.016 K km/s (Xb4d recovers only 55+-8% of the Xb4f flux: CH3OH is extended/resolved out at 0.9"); 5(-2,4)-4(-1,3) E (Eu 57 K): 0.035+-0.032 (Xb4f), 0.018+-0.015 (Xb4d), J=4..8 Q-branch <0.3. LTE (A, Trot) fit: Trot=9 K (1 sigma 8-9, 3 sigma 7-10 K) but chi2=53 for 6 dof: LTE is not a good description (Q J=1-3 under-predicted by 1.6x). RADEX (LAMDA e-ch3oh, n 1e2-1e8, Tkin 10-200 K, eta free) also fails (chi2min 55 for 5 dof; best Tkin=10 K, n>=1e7, N/eta degenerate). Conclusion: CH3OH rotational excitation is LOW (Trot<~15 K; Eu>45 K lines absent) or non-LTE; no useful density/column constraint; beam-averaged N_u(2_0, Eu=20 K)=1.7e12 cm-2 over 9.4x6.3" (N(E-CH3OH) of order 1e13-1e14 cm-2 for Trot~10 K, uncertain by >1 dex). Q-branch/2(0)-1(-1) ratio is the discriminator

results.quantity: H13CN 4-3 (345.340 GHz) upper limit with an explicit CO 3-2 wing model (Xb47 spw20 upper edge)
results.value: Template = HCN 4-3 profile of the region; CO wing fitted simultaneously (exponential, log-quadratic, log-cubic, power-law, Lorentzian; range 341.80-342.20 GHz; models with chi2/dof>1.3 rejected: Lorentzian, and the zero-CO case is excluded by chi2=695-1456 for 102 points). Accepted models: 3-sigma upper limit H13CN/HCN(4-3) < 0.09-0.11 (N), < 0.135-0.15 (S; log-quadratic/cubic only), < 0.075-0.15 (Bridge) i.e. HCN/H13CN > 9 (N), > 6.7 (S, Bridge); N best-fit alpha=0.015-0.045+-0.015 (<=3 sigma). Earlier zero-CO limits (0.15/0.45/0.24 from the half-profile) were looser but unmodelled. The limit is conditional on the wing family; with a free CO wing a real H13CN signal of this size is degenerate with the wing, so the limit is the minimum defensible; extending the fit to 342.28 GHz (CO core) gives similar numbers only for log-quadratic/cubic models
results.uncertainty: 3 sigma profile-likelihood (delta chi2=9)

results.quantity: Cross-check with the literature (Harada+2018 ApJ 855, 49, ALMA Band 3 line survey of NGC 3256; Sato+2022 A&A, APEX/NOEMA)
results.value: Agreements: CH3OH, SO, HOC+ and HCN/HCO+ detected there too; Harada+ report the largest chemical variation in CH3OH (and SiO), and CH3OH emission at the two nuclei "not dominant", more visible in tidal arms/outflow positions - consistent with our CH3OH peaking on the Bridge and W clump and being undetected at the N and S nuclei (<1.7% of HCO+) in Xb4d. HOC+ remains tentative here (3 sigma conservative) whereas Harada+ detect it at the central position (low-excitation lines). Not checked: SiO (not covered), H2CS (blended with CS 7-6 here, limit <0.34). Cross-check made from the published abstracts/summary only (tables not reproduced); status: partial

Minimum detectable N-S difference in a ladder ratio: ~30-40% (cross-band 14% x sqrt2 and ensemble spread), a 2-1 N-S HCN/HCO+ contrast is not measurable (N and S amplitudes correlated, corr ~0.8)

results.quantity: Q1b: Disk 3-2 deficit: resolved-out flux vs low excitation (parametric uv-hole model, Band 5 2-1 vs Band 6 Xb4f 3-2)

A Gaussian disk of FWHM th loses a fraction of its brightness exp[-(pi th B_min/lambda)^2/(4 ln2)] with B_min = 8.7 m (7-m array shadowing; both maps have B_max ~ lambda/theta_maj ~ 40 m, i.e. compact-array-like beams): deficit 0.76/0.67/0.58/0.49/0.33/0.18 for th = 10/12/14/16/20/25" (B_min 15 m: 0.44/0.31/0.20/0.12/0.04/0.006); the HCO+ deficit is reproduced by th = 13-14" (B_min 8.7 m) or 7-8" (15 m) -- a natural scale for the structure in the mask -- so the HCO+ disk deficit is fully consistent with the same excitation as the nuclei plus missing short spacings in Xb4f (MRS ~26" at 1.1 mm vs ~40" at 1.7 mm for B_min 8.7 m). Not consistent with the model alone: HCN (deficit 0.10 without correction, th=17-29" needed) and the double ratio (HCN/HCO+ 3-2)/(HCN/HCO+ 2-1) = 0.13 (none) / 0.54 (ring) in the disk vs 0.77 (N) and 0.76 (S) at 10": if HCN and HCO+ share distribution and recovery this double ratio is recovery-independent, so the disk HCN 3-2 is weak relative to HCO+ 3-2 (or HCN is more compact) -- but its value depends entirely on the ring zero level (0.13 vs 0.54). The robust disk number is HCN/HCO+ 2-1 = 0.47-0.50 (+-0.01 stat, +-0.03 zero level) vs 0.62 (N), 0.56 (S) at the same 10" beam, i.e. 15-25% lower; the disk 3-2 ratio is reported only as a lower limit in recovery (HCO+ 3-2/2-1 >= 0.265-0.287 true ratio)

results.quantity: Q3b: HCN blue-side excess at Soutflow over k*HCO+ and its independence from blends
results.value: HCN = k*HCO+ fitted on 2575-2875 km/s gives k=0.574+-0.019 (Michiyama South-OF-Blue position: 0.634+-0.021). The residual in HCN-frame 2375-2575 km/s is 0.164+-0.016 Jy/beam km/s = 57% of the HCN flux there (0.288); it is one broad bump (Gaussian centre 2497+-11, FWHM 211 km/s) of ~1 mJy/beam, 5-6 sigma per 50 km/s bin. Same excess in independent products: Xb4d tapered cube 0.238+-0.013 (73% of HCN), Xb4b smoothed to 1.05" 0.087+-0.026 (42%), significant (3 sigma per bin) only in 2500-2575. Blend test independent of the HCN wing: LTE forward models (Tex 15-120 K, line weights nu^3*S*mu2*exp(-Eu/T), HCO+-shaped or box velocity profile) of every in-band line of CH3NH2 (158 lines), CH3OH (59), CH2NH (54), CH3CHO (161), CH3SH (104) fitted to all other Band-6 channels at the same position (HCN/HCO+/SO channels and HOC+ masked) give no detection (A/sigma -1.3..+1.9) and 2-sigma upper bounds on the blend in HCN-frame 2375-2475 / 2475-2575 / 2575-2675 km/s of <=18% / <=10% / <=11% of the HCN flux (sum over species of the maximum over T and profile; Michiyama position <=37% / 13% / 11%); in the 2275-2375 bin (HCN weak, 0.6 mJy/beam) the bound is only <=42%. The CH3OH line at 263.728 GHz sky (rest 266.196 GHz, 3(2,1)-3(0,3)E) has log A=-8.5, ~1e-4 of the in-band CH3OH lines, so thermal CH3OH cannot contribute. HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) (266.161 GHz, Eu 157 K) has no other in-band line and is untestable (implausible but not excluded). Blend-corrected wing ratio therefore = R_obs*(1-f) with f<=0.1-0.2: e.g. blue half 1.24 -> 1.0-1.24. The earlier "10-15%" number is now derived (upper limit), not assumed. [Q13 (round 3): the excess is reproduced at matched beam and apertures at 4.4 sigma in Xb4d with a conservative null; Xb4b is consistent (not an independent confirmation: expected S/N <=2.5 at full recovery); HDO share <0.33-0.48 for HCO+-like kinematics and a >=7-17x lobe-specific enhancement for any other kinematics; see Q13a-Q13f.]
results.uncertainty: k +-0.02; blend fraction <=0.10-0.18 (2 sigma upper bound)

results.quantity: Q3b: kinematic test: outflow vs disk/warp/tidal feature at Soutflow
results.value: PV diagrams (out/q3b/q3b_pv.png, kin_ns_cuts.csv, kin_ew_cuts.csv). (1) The "sharp red edge" is NOT diagnostic: the 25%-of-peak red edge is 2867-2872 km/s at Soutflow, 2867-2889 at S and 2832-2889 along the N-S cut at x=-0.2": the lobe has no gas redder than the S disk red edge, i.e. it is one-sided (blue only), not specifically cut at Vsys+100. (2) E-W rotation gradient at the S declination 35 km/s/arcsec (v0=2795): expected line sigma for disk gas on the minor axis from beam smearing ~62 km/s, observed 130-150 (HCN) / 112-135 (HCO+) at Soutflow vs 24 at the W control (-4.4,-4.5) and 49-104 at the mirror N of S: the broadening is not rotation smearing. (3) HCO+/HCN peak velocity at Soutflow is 2806-2814, i.e. at the disk systemic velocity (narrow component, sigma 32), plus a broad blue-only skirt: centroid offset -125 km/s relative to the rotation-curve value (2769-2789); the skirt grows with distance from S (N-S centroid 2754 at -2.7", 2629 at -4.5", edge of emission ~-5.9"). (4) No blue tail at the mirror position N of S (blue half HCN 0.027+-0.006 vs 0.215+-0.010 Jy/beam km/s at Soutflow) nor at the W control, E control empty. (5) At 0.5" (Xb4b) the S-lobe pixel velocities scatter by 113 (HCO+)-262 (HCN) km/s rms with only a weak N-S gradient (+44+-5 / +27+-2 km/s/arcsec, r=0.15-0.21; E-W gradient -28..+15), i.e. clumps with up to ~100-250 km/s relative motions on <100 pc, not a smooth gradient (disk gradients here <~45 km/s/arcsec). Which predictions: a smooth warp/tidal arm predicts line widths set by the beam-smeared gradient (~60 km/s), velocities continuous with the E-W curve, and symmetric red/blue clumps; the data show one-sided broad blue gas with sigma 100-150 km/s, centroid shifted -100..-250 km/s and clump-to-clump scatter >100 km/s, which prefers an outflow/entrained or strongly perturbed gas. Not rejected: a tilted-ring warp with a PA twist and v_rot~250 km/s could project -100..-300 km/s on the minor axis, and a tidal feature. Classification stays MEDIUM: more consistent with the dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow (position/direction match Sakamoto+2014 and Michiyama+2018) than an isolated cloud, but disk-warp/tidal origin is an unrejected alternative.
results.uncertainty: centroid +-10-20 km/s

results.quantity: Q3b: classification of the Soutflow candidate (summary after round 2)
results.value: Soutflow (1.9" = 370 pc S of S) is detected in HCN (12.6 sigma) and HCO+ (5 sigma) at the position of the blue lobe of the southern edge-on outflow (within 0.6" of Michiyama South-OF-Blue). Kinematics: one-sided broad (sigma 100-150 km/s) blue-shifted gas (-100..-400 km/s) on top of a narrow disk-like component at systemic velocity; no blue tail at mirror or E-W control positions; clump velocity scatter >100 km/s. Classification: dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow, MEDIUM confidence; unrejected alternatives: tidal/warped disk gas. Chemistry: HCN/HCO+ 3-2 in the blue half 1.0-1.4 (fixed aperture; blend-corrected >=0.85-1.2), higher than S (0.46, >6 sigma), indistinguishable from N (1.13) and Bridge (1.3) in the same relative velocity bins; the broad component as a whole has 0.72-0.8; the "ratio 1.7-2" is a peak-selected, blue-tail value. results.quantity: Q4b: H13CN 4-3 N-nucleus "hint": null distribution at line-free control positions, injection-recovery, model mismatch, and reconciliation with team-b p0007
results.value: Same pipeline (5 wing models x 2 upper fit edges 342.20/342.28 GHz) at 34 line-free control positions (7-15" from the field centre, >=4.5" from sources) gives alpha = -0.04 to +0.001 mean, 0.015-0.036 scatter (models with a free wing are biased low). N alpha minus control mean: 0.04-0.11 for exp/log-quadratic/log-cubic/power-law wings (z_emp 2.1-3.9), but -0.016 to -0.02 (z=0) for the CO=HCO+-template wing and 0.00 for two other model/edge combinations (z -0.4 to +0.03): the "detection" survives only in some wing models, depends on the fit edge (z flips between 342.20 and 342.28 for exp and power-law wings), and mock tests with a shifted (+30 km/s) or broader (x1.25) true wing bias alpha by -0.02 to -0.11, comparable to the signal. Injection (alpha_inj=0.03/0.075 into N, S, Bridge and controls) is recovered to +-0.002 for the same-family wing, so the statistic is linear but model-mismatch dominated. VERDICT: not a detection (<=2-3 sigma, model dependent); empirical 3 sigma upper limits alpha<0.05-0.22 (flux) -> HCN/H13CN > 4.5-16 depending on model; conservative (all models, N) HCN/H13CN(4-3 flux) > 4.5, models with calibrated nulls consistent with p0007: >8 (power-law 10.8, exp 8.2 at 342.2; CO template 16). The earlier "+0.075, R~13" statement is retracted. Reconciliation with team-b p0007 (/snapshots/team-b-s04, s41/s49): they quote HCN/H13CN > 8.3 from a 5-wing-model profile-likelihood plus 144-realisation injection; our Q4 value (N >8.3) agrees numerically; our wider empirical-null range (>4.5) is more conservative because it includes log-polynomial wings that absorb the line. Both teams agree: opacity-vs-abundance is not decided by H13CN, because RADEX keeps HCN/H13CN(4-3) Tb >= 0.73*A even at tau 100-800.

results.quantity: Q4c: Independent prediction test: classes fitted WITHOUT any J=1-0 datum predict the 1-0 ratios
results.value: Fit of HCN/HCO+ ladders (3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2, both lines) and R32 only (5 data), then prediction of R10 and the single-line 3-2/1-0 ratios (95% posterior range; physT30). S: A (both thick, equal filling, different Tex): R10 = 0.59 [0.57-1.10], HCN 3-2/1-0 0.26 [0.22-0.30], HCO+ 3-2/1-0 0.41 [0.35-0.68]; B (both thick, same Tex, HCN filling smaller, kappa 0.4): R10 = 0.43 [0.39-0.59], 0.30, 0.35; F2 (separate n): 0.61 [0.55-1.03]. Observed S: R10 0.645+-0.013 (Harada) / 0.60+-0.08 (Michiyama), HCN 3-2/1-0 0.335+-0.028, HCO+ 3-2/1-0 0.55+-0.06. => B under-predicts R10 by 0.2 (outside its 95% range) and is DISFAVOURED; A and F2 reproduce R10 (A inside its 95% range) but under-predict both 3-2/1-0 ratios by 2.3-2.5 sigma (3-2 flux scale or 3-2 excitation). N: A 0.82 [0.74-1.36], B 0.76 [0.68-1.16], F2 0.84 [0.65-1.03] vs observed 0.961 (0.94+-0.13): all under-predict by ~0.1-0.2. The thin classes predict R10 0.88 (C) and 1.46 (D) at S, and HCO+ 3-2/1-0 of 1.7-1.8 (observed 0.55). Because kappa<1 (B) lowers R10 and R32 by the same factor, only the ratio-of-ratios (excitation) can raise 3-2 relative to 1-0: the data prefer a model in which the J=1-0 contrast is real, not filling-driven.
results.uncertainty: 95% posterior ranges; 0-1 dof

results.quantity: Q4c: Joint RADEX model comparison incl. 1-0 data and a separate-density class: S and N
results.value: chi2 / BIC / ln(marginal likelihood), physT30 prior, all 8 data (S): A both thick kappa=1: 9.9 / 20.3 / -15.5; B both thick same Tex kappa free: 12.4 / 24.9 / -20.3; C HCN thin: 87.2 / 97.6 / -55.3; D both thin: 74.9 / 85.3 / -49.2; F separate n (common Tkin), kappa free: 7.9 / 22.5 / -18.6; F2 separate n, kappa=1: 7.9 / 20.4 / -16.3. N: A 23.2 / 33.6 / -22.6; B 19.3 / 31.7 / -23.3; C 374 / 385; D 304 / 314; F 19.1 / 33.7 / -23.8; F2 19.3 / 31.8 / -22.0. => A and F2 are preferred at S (odds A:F2 ~2:1, A:B ~100:1, A:F ~20:1 in marginal likelihood; Delta BIC B-A = 4.6); separate densities for HCN and HCO+ do not improve the fit enough to be required (chi2 -2.0 for 1 extra parameter), and it is NOT decidable between A and F2. Thin classes are rejected (Delta chi2 >= 64 (physT30; >= 28 for the grid prior)) with the 1-0 data included, also WITHOUT the Band-5 2-1 ratios (S: A 6.6, B 9.5, C 77.9, D 70.9, F 5.1; grid prior with Tkin from 8 K: A 6.1, C 34, D 53), so the rejection no longer rests on the 2-1 deblend. If BOTH the 2-1 and the 1-0 information are dropped (4 data) the thin classes are allowed again at the grid prior (S: A 2.1, C 3.3, D 4.0) and only D is disfavoured at Tkin>=30 K (6.8): the rejection of thin HCN comes from the J=1-0 data (3-2/1-0 ratios and R10), i.e. from sub-thermal excitation of thick gas. N is badly fitted by every class (chi2 19-23 for 8 data, 3-4 dof): a single (n,T) component does not describe the N nucleus (compact core + envelope), so statements about N are conditional on an inadequate model. Two-component (compact thick core + extended thin gas) models were not fitted: 8 data cannot constrain 8+ parameters; the dilution fit (entry Q4b: Beam-filling) gives the sizes (0.45-0.56" FWHM). [SUPERSEDED STATISTIC: this chi2/BIC used 8 data of which R32 is algebraically redundant (R32=R10*(H32/10)/(O32/10)) and a 'physT30'/grid prior with fixed geometry; the Q12c fit statistic (7 independent data, profile chi2 incl. nuisance penalties, calibrated by simulation) replaces it: one-zone N chi2 9.1/3 dof (p=0.028) at fixed geometry, 3.2/3 (p=0.36) with measured geometry priors. Treat the 19-23/8 numbers as a relative ranking of classes only.]
results.uncertainty: ln Z prior dependent (flat in log on the grid); see csv

results.quantity: Q4c: Which parameter changes between N and S? Differential fit with common (Tkin, n)
results.value: Both nuclei fitted simultaneously (both thick; kappa=1; physT30; 8 data per nucleus, 16 total; BIC with 2x8 data). chi2 (npar): nothing changes 121.8 (4); kappa(S) differs 52.1 (5; best kappa_S=0.75); N(HCN) differs 43.9 (5; best logN(HCN) N 16.75, S 16.50 at common T=65 K, log n=4.25, logN(HCO+)=16.0); N(HCO+) differs 44.1 (5); both columns differ 43.9 (6); n differs 107.1 (5); Tkin differs 90.8 (5); independent fits 33.1 (8). BIC: independent 55.3, N(HCN) differs 57.7, N(HCO+) differs 57.9, kappa(S) 65.9, Tkin 104.7, n 121.0, nothing 132.9. Without the 2-1 ratios (12 data): nothing 97.7, kappa 36.2, N(HCN) 27.5, N(HCO+) 30.7, n 74.8, Tkin 56.8, independent 15.8 (BIC 35.7 vs 39.9 / 43.2 / 48.7). Profile of the HCN column shift (S minus N, other parameters common): -0.25 dex (1 sigma -0.5 to -0.25 without 2-1; grid step 0.25 dex). => The data need a change of the HCN (or HCO+) column ratio at S by a factor 1.8-3; a change in density or temperature alone is excluded (Delta chi2 29-63 worse than the column option) and a filling change (kappa 0.75) is worse by Delta chi2 8 (Delta BIC 8). A common-column model does not fit either nucleus pair (chi2 121.8/12 dof) and even the best one-parameter option has chi2 44/11 dof, so N and S differ by more than one parameter (independent fits: Delta chi2 = 11 for 3 more parameters). Interpretation: the factor 2 at 3-2 is mostly a column/abundance (or optical-depth) difference of HCN relative to HCO+, which cannot be told apart from the abundance ratio by these data.
results.uncertainty: grid step 0.25 dex

results.quantity: Q4c: Physical quantities with a single-cloud line width (dv=50 km/s) and consistency with CO-based clouds
results.value: RADEX depends on N/dv (direct dv=50 runs at N/3 give identical T_R, tau, Tex: out/q4c/phys_dv_check.csv), so tau, Tex and the ordering A,B,F >> C,D are unchanged and all columns scale: N(HCN) per cloud = N(HCN,dv=150)/3. S, class A: N(HCN) = 10^16.67 (10^16.0-16.75) at dv=150, i.e. 10^16.19 per 54-km/s cloud (Brunetti+2022 median cloud sigma 23 km/s -> FWHM 54) with ~3 non-overlapping clouds needed along the line of sight to build the observed ~150 km/s line (more if clouds overlap in velocity: then RADEX per-cloud tau/Tex are changed by inter-cloud coupling, not modelled). Class F2 S: 10^16.5 (10^15.25-16.75) -> 10^16.0 per cloud; N, A: 10^16.0 (10^16.0-16.75) -> 10^15.5. n(H2) 10^4.5 (10^4.25-10^5.25), Tkin 30 (30-50) K at S (A); thermal P/k = n T = 10^5.98 (10^5.75-10^6.72) = 1e6 (6e5-5e6) K cm-3 at S, 10^6.74 (1e6-6e6) at N: below the median internal turbulent pressure 1e7 K cm-3 of the CO clouds (Brunetti+2022; range 1e5-1e10 in Brunetti+2021) by 1.8-10x (inside the range of the CO clouds); but if the dense gas had the cloud sigma of 23 km/s its turbulent pressure at that n would be P_turb/k ~ 6e9-1e10, 1e3 above the cloud median, so the dense gas is consistent only with being self-gravitating/transient or with a dispersion of <~1 km/s. N(H2)=N(HCN)/X(HCN): for X=1e-8 (assumed; 1e-9..1e-7) S class A N(H2) 5e24 (1e24-6e24) cm-2 = Sigma 1.1e5 (2e4-1.2e5) Msun/pc2 (with He, 2.17e-20 Msun/pc2 per cm-2; N: 2e4, 2e3 for X=1e-7), against CO Sigma 8-5500 Msun/pc2 at 55-120 pc (median 470 at 90 pc, Brunetti+2021/22): TENSION of 4-20x (100% of the S/A posterior above 5500 for X=1e-8, 74% for X=1e-7; N/A 100%/23%); it vanishes only for X(HCN) >~ 2e-7 (or a RADEX n or HCN column over-estimated by the single-zone model). Equivalently, Sigma <= 5500 implies a dense-gas path <= 3 pc at n = 3e4, i.e. a volume filling of <~3% over 90 pc, whereas for X=1e-8 the path N(H2)/n is ~58 pc (prior-capped at 100 pc; the earlier "filling 1-30%" statement refers to this and is superseded). Sky filling eta 0.6-0.9 (A, S) and a large volume-filling are not simultaneously consistent with Sigma_CO; this is flagged as a tension, not explained.
results.uncertainty: see csv (95% posterior)

results.quantity: Q4c: CS 7-6 as a discriminator between HCO+ enhancement and HCN deficit
results.value: Data (Q1 deblend with 1" templates, matched coarse beam, Tb; spread of the template ensemble + 14% cross-band): CS 7-6/HCO+ 3-2 N 0.051+-0.014, S 0.056+-0.019 (S/N = 1.09+-0.48); CS 7-6/HCN 3-2 N 0.077+-0.016, S 0.149+-0.050 (S/N = 1.93+-0.75, i.e. HCN/CS is 1.9x lower at S, 1.2 sigma). At low J (Harada Table 13, 1.7"): CS(2-1)/HCO+(1-0) N 0.239+-0.003, S 0.261+-0.008 (S/N 1.09), HCN(1-0)/CS(2-1) N 4.03, S 2.47 (S/N 0.61+-0.03), HNC(1-0)/HCN(1-0) N 0.559, S 0.495 (HNC/HCO+ N 0.537, S 0.320). Model (CS 7-6 RADEX at the HCO+ Tkin, n; N(CS) solved from the observed CS/HCO+ ratio per posterior draw): S minus N log[N(HCN)/N(CS)] = -0.51 (-0.69..-0.32; 2.8 sigma) in class A, -0.11 (0.6 sigma) in B, +0.16 (0.2 sigma) in F2; log[N(HCO+)/N(CS)] -0.26 (1.3 sigma) / +0.02 / -0.20. Verdict: from CS 7-6 alone UNDECIDED (model dependent, <=1.2 sigma in the data, 0.2-2.8 sigma in the models). The low-J literature data are model-light and point the same way: HCO+ and CS track each other at N and S, HCN (and HNC) are lower at S, i.e. they FAVOUR an HCN (N-bearing) deficit over an HCO+ enhancement, tentatively, provided CS(2-1) and HCO+(1-0) are excited similarly at N and S (not tested). This replaces both earlier statements: the Q1 sentence "CS tracks HCO+ not HCN" is the above, weak (1.2 sigma) result, and the Q4b "CS/HCO+ 4-3 0.047 S vs 0.081 N (factor 1.7)" came from undeblended peak pixels of the 4.1x2.7" beam (N and S partly blended) and is withdrawn.

results.quantity: Q4c: SO scope and shock-tracer statements (corrected)
results.value: Beam matching verified in the script (q4_so.py): SO 4_5-3_4 (Xb55, native 9.4x6.3"), SO 6_5-5_4 (251.826 GHz; Xb4f, native 5.7x3.5") and SO 8_8-7_7 (Xb47, 4.1x2.7") are all convolved channel-wise to 9.4x6.3" PA -88 and sampled at the field centre (RA0, DE0), so the ratio is a central-beam (N+S+Bridge; 9x6" = 1.8x1.2 kpc at 194 pc/arcsec) average, NOT a nuclear value. Source-size assumption (Trot limit 95/99.7%, thin LTE, 14% calibration; f = Xb4f recovery; r = area of the 6_5-5_4 emission / area of the 4_5-3_4 emission): equal extent r=1: f=1 12.4/15.3 K, f=0.7 14.9/19.3, f=0.5 18.5/25.7; r=0.5: 18.4/25.7, 24.4/39.2, 36/80; r=0.25: 36/79, 70/>300, >300; the 8_8-7_7 limit is weaker (f=1,r=1: 19.6/28.8 K; r=0.25: 35/79). Hence "SO Trot<~12-25 K" holds only for SO that is equally extended in its 24-K and 51-K lines; a compact warm (Trot >= 30-80 K) SO component within the 9" beam is NOT excluded, and the statement "no shock signature at the nuclei" is withdrawn for SO. SO/HCO+(2-1) = 0.020+-0.003 (central beam) cannot be compared with Harada SO(2_1-3_2, 99.3 GHz)/HCO+(1-0) = 0.024+-0.004 (N), 0.069+-0.009 (S) at 1.7" (different SO line and beam; there is no shock-free-starburst SO/HCO+ benchmark taken from a paper here). Naming: Harada's "SO 6_5-5_4" is at 219.949 GHz (N: SO/HCO+(3-2)=0.026+-0.008; not in our bands), ours is 251.826 GHz. The stronger shock tracer is CH3OH: CH3OH 2(0)-1(-1)/HCO+ 3-2 at 0.95" N <0.013, S <0.017, Bridge 0.052+-0.006 (ours), and at 1.7" Harada CH3OH 2k-1k(96.7)/HCO+(1-0) N 0.015+-0.003, S 0.071+-0.008 (S/N = 4.7; ours at 6": S/N 3.5): CH3OH rises towards S on 1.7-6" scales but not at the S peak pixel at 0.95", i.e. it is extended off-nuclear gas. HOC+(1-0)/HCO+(1-0) (Harada) N 0.019+-0.005, S 0.034+-0.011; SiO(2-1)/HCO+(1-0) 0.031 at both (compare our HOC+/HCO+ 3-2 N 0.054+-0.016, S <0.098: different J, tentative).

results.quantity: Q4c: HCN v2=1f: vibrational temperature limit and comparison with CON/obscured nuclei
results.value: Ratio limits Tb(v2=1f)/Tb(v=0) (3 sigma): 3-2 at 0.24" N <0.059, S <0.080; 0.95" N <0.030, S <0.048; 6" N <0.024, S <0.049; 4-3 (4.1x2.7") N <0.028, S <0.087; population ratio N(v2=1)/N(v=0) <0.03-0.15 (optically thin vib line, equal filling) => Tvib < 290-380 K (N) and 350-430 K (S) (upper end 540 K for the weakest bound), E(v2=1)=1024 K, alpha = 0.86 exp(-1024/Tvib) (team-b: Tvib < 270-360 K, N). Published Tvib: NGC 4418 ~230 K (Sakamoto+2010, arXiv:1011.6449), Mrk 231 200-400 K (Aalto+2015b, arXiv:1411.2474), IRAS 17208, Arp 220, IC 860, Zw049.057 with buried nuclei of >5e13 Lsun/kpc2 (Aalto+2015a, arXiv:1504.06824; abstracts read). Our limit excludes Tvib >~ 300-430 K at N and S but NOT 200-300 K: an IR-pumped HCN (14 um) like NGC 4418 would give alpha = 0.005-0.03 and is not excluded; the earlier "no IR pumping" is replaced by "no vibrationally excited HCN above alpha 0.03-0.09 (Tvib < 290-430 K)". The limit is for the peak pixel; a nucleus smaller than 47 pc (the 0.24" beam) is diluted. The 4.7 um continuum of the S nucleus (Pereira-Santaella+2024, JWST; abstract level only) implies a hot embedded source, so a 14-um pumping test needs the mid-IR brightness temperature, which is not available here.

Harada Tables 5 and 6 (rotation-diagram column densities and Tex; two N/Tex pairs are printed per species, the HTML parse lost their labels): HCN N 2.4e14 (Tex 6.0 K) and 1.5e14 (6.1 K) at N, 8.8e13 (5.6 K) and 4.9e13 (5.8 K) at S; HCO+ N 1.3e14 (6.5 K) and 1.0e14 (6.9 K), S 8.5e13 (6.7 K) and 4.3e13 (7.3 K). NOT verified: HCN vib/ground, SO/HCO+, CH3OH/HCO+ in NGC 253, Arp 220, NGC 1068, so our limits are not placed against them; no shock-free starburst SO/HCO+ benchmark was taken from a paper.

results.quantity: Q4c: Q4 summary: origin of the factor-2 lower HCN/HCO+ 3-2 at S (final, differential)
results.value: SUPPORTED (low-medium confidence; 1-4 dof): (1) The contrast is only partly J-dependent: N/S = 1.49 at J=1-0 vs 1.9-2.0 at 3-2 (1.7"), so ~60% (log) of it is J-independent. (2) Joint RADEX fits including the 1-0 data prefer both lines thick with HCN more sub-thermal than HCO+ (class A: Tex 7 vs 11 K, HCN tau32 >~10; or separate densities F2, indistinguishable), and reject thin-HCN/abundance-only classes (C, D; Delta chi2 >= 64 (physT30; >= 28 for the grid prior)), independently of the Band-5 2-1 ratios; class B (different filling at equal Tex) fails the independent 1-0 prediction (0.43 vs 0.645). HCN tau32 > ~2 (95%), no upper limit. (3) Between N and S the data need a change of the HCN (or HCO+) column ratio by a factor 1.8-3 (logN(HCN) -0.25 to -0.5 dex), not of n or Tkin (Delta chi2 29-63 worse) and not only of filling (Delta chi2 8 worse). (4) CS/low-J data weakly favour an HCN (N-bearing) deficit over an HCO+ enhancement (HCO+/CS equal at N and S; HCN/CS and HNC/HCO+ lower at S) but CS 7-6 modelling is undecided (0.2-2.8 sigma). (5) IR pumping: no HCN v2=1f above alpha 0.03-0.09 (Tvib < 290-430 K), which does not exclude CON-like Tvib 200-300 K. (6) Shocks: SO (central 9x6" beam only) Trot < 12-25 K if equally extended, not excluded for compact warm gas; CH3OH is extended/off-nuclear (nuclei <0.013/<0.017 at 0.95"). NOT decided: excitation (A) vs separate densities (F2), HCN opacity upper range, abundance vs optical depth, HCO+ enhancement vs HCN deficit (tentative HCN deficit), whether N (poorly fitted, chi2 19-23/8) is a valid calibration. TENSION: with X(HCN)=1e-8 the HCN column implies Sigma 2e4-1e5 Msun/pc2, 4-20x above the CO maximum (5500); needs X(HCN) >~ 2e-7 or a clumped geometry the one-zone RADEX does not describe. Discriminating observations: HCN 1-0/3-2 and H13CN at <=0.3" (alpha < 0.03), HCN 6-5/7-6, HCO+ and CS at matched high J. [SUPERSEDED STATISTIC: this chi2/BIC used 8 data of which R32 is algebraically redundant (R32=R10*(H32/10)/(O32/10)) and a 'physT30'/grid prior with fixed geometry; the Q12c fit statistic (7 independent data, profile chi2 incl. nuisance penalties, calibrated by simulation) replaces it: one-zone N chi2 9.1/3 dof (p=0.028) at fixed geometry, 3.2/3 (p=0.36) with measured geometry priors. Treat the 19-23/8 numbers as a relative ranking of classes only.]

results.quantity: Is the 1.05" N wing rise / ratio-vs-velocity slope a beam (spatial-mixing) effect? Matched-aperture, matched-beam, centroid and injection tests
results.value: Same aperture r<0.5" about N, 40-km/s bins over +-140 km/s, no mask: weighted linear slope Xb4d@1.05" +0.082+-0.006 per 100 km/s (chi2/dof const 221/6); Xb4b convolved to 1.05" +0.072+-0.008 (92/6) -> the two arrays agree (difference 1.0 sigma, so not an Xb4b-recovery effect); Xb4b at native-like 0.30" +-0.003+-0.013 (12/6, mean 0.875). Same data, same aperture, only the beam changes -> the slope is generated by the 1.05" beam. Injection (HCN = R(r_N)*HCO+ on the Xb4b HCO+ cube, R from the measured profile 0.98/0.82/0.63/0.48/0.40 at r=0.125/0.375/0.75/1.5/3", identical kinematics, smoothed to 1.05"): predicted slope +0.049 per 100 km/s (mean 0.78 vs observed 0.77): i.e. ~60-70% of the observed slope arises from a purely radial ratio gradient + velocity gradient, none from spectral variation; residual +0.02-0.03 per 100 km/s (3 sigma) is not reproduced (steeper unresolved central R(r) or genuine red-wing HCN excess). Centroids (HCN minus HCO+ per 40 km/s bin, r<1.2", Xb4d): dx = +0.04..+0.06" (blue), -0.001 (0), -0.09 (+80), -0.125+-0.034" (+120 km/s); Xb4b 0.30": +0.02 -> -0.038+-0.003" (+80); dy <=0.04": HCN emission is systematically closer to the nucleus than HCO+ at every velocity (HCO+ centroid moves -0.5" -> +0.28" across the line), with a larger offset on the red side, consistent with an HCN-richer compact core mixed in a 1.05" beam with lower-ratio extended gas
results.uncertainty: slopes +-0.006-0.013; centroid errors from S/N (0.6 FWHM/SNR) + no systematic astrometry; injection input R(r) measured at 0.30" so central gradient underestimated

results.quantity: Q12c (HEADLINE): does a compact-core + envelope two-component non-LTE model fix the N one-zone fit and change the S result; is the N-vs-S temperature contrast significant?
results.value: No second component is required, and none is excluded. (1) With 7 independent data the one-zone N fit is marginal only if the beam geometry is held fixed (profile chi2 9.1/3 dof, p=0.028); with the geometry (extended filling at 1.7", compact size) given the widths measured from the 0.25/0.95/1.7/5.7" Tb growth curve it is acceptable (chi2 3.2/3, p=0.36; 1.5-3.2, p=0.36-0.67 over the measured-geometry variants). (2) The Bayesian preference for two components at N (dlnZ(2cT-1z)=+3.0, fixed geometry) vanishes with measured geometry (-1.7), with the 25% error floor (+1.2) and with judgement geometry widths (-0.2 to +0.7); in simulations the +3 threshold is exceeded by 14.5% [10-20%] of data-consistent one-zone truths with wrong sizes, so it is not significant; with measured-geometry priors the statistic has no power to separate the truths (two-comp truths give dlnZ -1.0 to -1.2, one-zone truths -0.4 to -2.1). (3) S: one-zone adequate (chi2 5.2/3, p=0.16; measured geometry 3.1/3), dlnZ -0.8 to +0.4; Tkin 19-23 K (16-84% 14-35 K), Tbg<=5 K branch unchanged (20 K [14,32] at Tbg 5 K), P(T>=80 K)<=0.06. N compact Tkin is unconstrained (12-96 K; 62 [39,96] fixed-geometry one-zone, 15 [12,25] measured-geometry one-zone, 27 [14,70] two-comp). (4) Delta T = T_N - T_S is unconstrained: joint draw-by-draw over 16 deblend variants P(T_N>T_S)=0.47-0.60 with measured geometry (variant range 0.23-0.88), 0.72-0.93 at fixed geometry; Delta T median -0.5..+4 K [16-84%: -10, +36] with measured geometry, +10..+35 K at fixed geometry. (5) H13CN 4-3 removes 50-80% of the N two-comp posterior mass (survival 0.20-0.50) and S 20-30%; compact tau32 median 23-37 -> 5-14 at N; the strongest earlier claim (n_c>1e6, tau32 10-100) is not robust.
results.uncertainty: see sub-results

results.value: Fit with fixed geometry ('base'): P(dlnZ>=3) = 0/200 (95% upper bound 1.8%) if the truth is the one-zone best fit with the assumed geometry; 29/200 = 14.5% (9.9-20.2%) if the truth is a one-zone model with 2-1 compact size x1.35 and 4-3 x0.74 that still fits the observed N data (chi2 4.4/3); 0/200 for the opposite shift (x0.74/x1.35: not data-consistent, chi2 28.5). Power: 54.5% (two-component truth, same geometry), 33% (two-comp, u=2, refit to data), 52% (u=0.5). The observed +3.02 is exceeded in 14.5% of the data-consistent geometry-mis-specified one-zone simulations (p=0.145; 0.00 for the correctly specified one). With the measured-geometry priors the statistic is negative for all truths (median over simulations: one-zone truths -2.1 to +0.1, two-comp truths u=2/0.5: -1.0/-1.2; P(dlnZ>=3)=0/200 for every truth) and the observed -1.67 lies at P(dlnZ>=obs)=0.37-0.97, i.e. the data have no power to separate one from two components once geometry is free (the dlnZ distributions of the two-component and one-zone truths overlap). Chi2 of the one-zone fit: P(chi2>=9.1)=0.015 (right geometry), 0.30 (mis-specified geometry), 0.49-0.68 (two-component truths).

results.quantity: Q8d: source-model uv forward model calibrated on the three Band-6 arrays (Xb4b, Xb4d, Xb4f; line and continuum): effective short-baseline limits and the predicted Xb47-vs-Xb4f recovery
results.value: Model: each position = compact + extended circular Gaussian (4 free parameters per position and line; continuum 3), seen through a short-baseline high-pass (Gaussian taper, taper without dirty-beam normalisation, or sharp cut) with a 'largest scale kept' L = 0.53 lambda/Bmin; Xb47 and Xb55 share the Xb4f configuration (Bmin ratio lognormal(0,0.25)); 70 calibration data (native-beam 3-2 peaks of Xb4b/Xb4d/Xb4f + 1.7", Xb4d/Xb4f and Xb4b/Xb4f 3-2 ratios at 3 matched beams, continuum Xb4d/Xb4f, Xb4b/Xb4f at 2 beams) and 40 parameters, emcee. All six fits reproduce the calibration data (chi2_min 51-66 for 70 data; posterior-predictive Xb4d/Xb4f HCN N 0.86 S 0.71 Bridge 0.80, Xb4b/Xb4f N 0.75 S 0.58 vs observed 0.875 0.720 0.809 / 0.792 0.601 0.651). The data fix the ARRAY ORDER robustly (Xb4f least lossy) but the ABSOLUTE loss of Xb4f/Xb47 depends on the prior on Bmin: (A) unbounded L (data-preferred): L_f >= 24" (36 [24,50]), L_d 15.5 [13.4,17.1]", L_b 13.4 [11.8,14.7]" -> Xb4f and Xb47 ~lossless; this needs Bmin(Xb4f) ~3 m, below the 12 m dish diameter: physically impossible. (B) physical Bmin>=15 m (L<=8.2" at 266 GHz): L_f at the cap (7.8-8.1"), L_d 6.3 [6.0,6.5]" (Bmin ~20 m), L_b 5.7 [5.4,5.9]" (~22 m), L_47 5.2 [4.4,5.9]" (cap 6.2"); chi2 +14 (taper) or +2 (taper without normalisation) relative to A; the sharp-cut variant is rejected by the continuum spectral-index bound (see below). Predicted 3-2 peak recovery at the Xb4f beam: A: Xb4f 0.99 N, 0.94 S; Xb47(4-3)/Xb4f(3-2) = 0.98 N, 0.95 S, 0.97 Bridge. B: Xb4f 0.62-0.87 N, 0.17-0.23 S (an extended envelope invisible to all arrays); Xb47/Xb4f = 0.68-0.74 N, 0.52-0.54 S, 0.61-0.65 Bridge (equal compact/extended excitation). Constraint from the continuum: Xb47/Xb4f continuum 2.29 N, 1.91 S, 2.18 Bridge implies spectral index alpha(258-347 GHz) = 2.9 N, 2.3 S, 2.7 Bridge in A and 4.0-4.2 N, 3.8-4.0 S, 4.3-4.5 Bridge in B (sharp cut: 5-8, impossible for dust+free-free); draws with alpha outside [1.5,4.5] are removed (B keeps 52-63%, sharp-cut B 0%).
results.uncertainty: model-dependent: Xb47/Xb4f peak recovery 0.52-0.74 (physical) to 0.95-0.98 (unbounded); differential N-vs-S loss 1.0 (unbounded) to 1.3-1.4 (physical); the 4-3 sizes are assumed equal to the 3-2 sizes (or compact x0.7)

results.quantity: Q8f: Tkin vs density vs size: what the contrast means physically, with both interpretations
results.value: Pure size/filling difference with equal excitation (compact+extended Gaussians with the fitted N and S sizes) gives HCN contrast 1.02-1.13 (P(>=1.33)<=0.1 for plausible r_e; Q8 round 1, scripts/q8_forward.py), so size alone does not make N look more excited; the remaining effects are recovery (Q8d-e) and real excitation. Extended-component T43/T32 (the component that carries 70-97% of the Xb4f/Xb47-beam peak: compact share of the unfiltered 3-2 peak at the Xb4f beam N 0.15-0.22, S 0.03-0.16, Bridge 0.08-0.17) solved from the observed ratios: physical family HCN r_ext N 0.57, S 0.54 (HCO+ 0.75, 0.78); unbounded family HCN N 0.43, S 0.31 (HCO+ 0.57, 0.51). RADEX one-zone inversion (logN(HCN)=15.5, equal n, T from the ratio): physical family T_N/T_S = 1.2 [0.96,1.43] (log n=6; HCN), 1.3 at log n=5.5; HCO+ 0.83 [0.63,1.04]; unbounded family T_N/T_S = 1.7 [1.4,1.9] (log n=6) to 1.9 [1.5,2.2] (log n=5), e.g. 38 vs 22 K at n=1e6; HCO+ 1.2-1.6. Overall T_N/T_S ~ 0.8-1.9, consistent with 1, with a face-value upper end of ~1.9 that needs a lossless Xb4f/Xb47, which the minimum-baseline argument disfavours; at equal T the corresponding density difference is Tkin-degenerate (0.2-0.4 dex in n). Compact (nuclear) component alone: it carries only 3-21% of the 4-3 peak at the Xb4f beam, and its T43/T32 is unconstrained by these data (if the extended gas has a common ratio 0.30, the compact N/S ratio needed is 1.8 in the unbounded family, 1.04-1.3 in the physical family with r_c>1.5 i.e. unphysical unless r_ext>=0.45): a nuclear excitation difference is allowed but not required.
results.uncertainty: T_N/T_S 0.8-1.9 depending on the uv family; extended-gas ratios +-0.05; one-zone RADEX, T-n degeneracy remains

results.quantity: Q8h: what a matched ~1" 1-0 (or 2-1 at Xb4d resolution) map would add (not in the archive)
results.value: The archive has 2-1 only at 9x6" (Xb55), 3-2 at 0.25/0.95/6" and 4-3 only at 4.2x2.7" (Xb47): no common-uv ladder exists. A 1-0 or 2-1 map at ~1" from the same configuration as a 4-3 map would (i) give the T-n degeneracy a third step, (ii) allow recovery to be calibrated on a ladder with the same Bmin/lambda, and (iii) resolve the compact component (0.4") from the extended gas at N. Without it the compact-component excitation is unconstrained and the N-S contrast is bounded to N/S <= 1.4 (95%, corrected) rather than measured.

results.quantity: Q14g: matched comparison with Harada+2018 (CH3OH 2k-1k 96.74 GHz / HCO+ 3-2 at 1.7"): data facts, matched-estimator prediction and which explanation is allowed
results.value: HARADA SETUP (paper, Table 1-3): CH3OH 96.74 comes from Band3_c (94.7-98.3 GHz) 12-m ONLY (PI data 2015.1.00412.S/2016.1.00965.S C36-2/3, baselines 14.6-628 m, plus archive 2015.1.00993.S C36-2/3, 13.6-428 m; no ACA at Band 3; the earlier statement 'ACA-including Band 3' was wrong), imaged 1.68x1.62" (rob1, rms 17.9 mJy/beam km/s); HCO+ 3-2 is 12-m C36-2/3 (13.7-412 m) + 7-m ACA (9-44.5 m), 0.94x0.90"; all spectra convolved to 1.7" circular, integral = sum over +-150 km/s about 2775 km/s with no baseline fit (error dI dv sqrt(N), N for 300 km/s); Table 13 values: CH3OH 2k-1k N 3.09+-0.66, S 6.22+-0.66 K km/s; HCO+ 3-2 N 91.56, S 43.69 (our Xb4d at 1.7", +-150 km/s: N 86.0, S 53.7: -6%, +23%); 241.79 5k-4k N 5.84+-0.57, S 4.35+-0.57; 254.015 is not in Table 13 at N/S (<2 sigma peak). Shortest 12-m baselines 13.6-14.6 m at 96.7 GHz give MRS ~0.6 lambda/B = 28" (ours at 254 GHz: Xb4d min baseline not in headers; Xb4f beam 6.3x3.8" at 265 GHz implies B_max~45 m, i.e. a compact/ACA-like array, inferred not verified). OUR ESTIMATOR LADDER at S, 1.7" (K km/s of 254.015): window moment (+-150 km/s, local baseline) 0.447+-0.17 (empirical null 0.16-0.28) -> whole-line HCO+-template fit with SiS 14-13 and 30SiO 6-5 in the same window 0.694 (S/N 2.6) -> + feathering with the low-resolution deficit D=[Xb4f-Xb4d] at 6.3x3.8" (+0.19+-0.11 S, +0.03 N) 0.877+-0.285; N: 0.226 -> 0.370+-0.24 -> 0.396+-0.26. The +-150 km/s window contains 97% (S) / 99% (N) of the line. PREDICTED 96.74 (K km/s; LTE at Harada's OWN Trot from 241.79/96.74 = 0.70 (S) -> 11.1 (10.4-11.8) K, 1.89 (N) -> 17.3 (15.5-19.9) K; R96/254 = 5.96 (S), 5.36 (N), CMB contrast included): S Xb4d-only 4.14+-1.59 (0.67 of Harada, -1.2 sigma), feathered 5.23+-1.70 (0.84, -0.5 sigma; to Harada's HCO+ 0.120 vs 0.142+-0.015); N Xb4d-only 1.98+-1.29 (0.64), feathered 2.12+-1.39 (0.69, -0.6 sigma; ratio 0.023 vs 0.034+-0.007). Using R96/254 = 4.9-6.6 (Trot 8-30 K) changes this by <=15%. Non-LTE (RADEX constrained by R(254/Q-blend) and Harada's 241.79/96.74): N R96/254 = 8.6 (7.5-12) -> pred 3.2-3.4 (1.0-1.1 of Harada, +0.1 sigma); S R96/254 = 23 (20-27) -> pred 15-23 (2.5-3.6x Harada, +1.5-2.2 sigma; this S solution is itself a poor joint fit, chi2=8.9 for the 2 ratios, which refer to different beams). VERDICT: the previous 'x3 tension' (pred 0.04-0.05 vs 0.142 at 1.7") came from the window-limited moment at 1.7" with a +-50% error; with the matched whole-line estimator the LTE prediction agrees with Harada within ~1 sigma at both nuclei (pred/Harada 0.64-0.84). Which of the three explanations is allowed: (1) uv coverage - allowed and measured but not dominant: feathering adds +26% (S) / +7% (N); the 12-m data recover 98+-16% (R<=3") to 64+-10% (R=6") of Xb4f CH3OH flux at S (Q14j); (2) aperture/position - not required; shifting the 1.7" aperture by <=0.5"/1" changes the feathered S 254 to 0.86/1.13 K km/s (window estimator), i.e. a <=1" pointing difference can by itself supply the residual 20%; (3) excitation - LTE at Harada's own Trot suffices; high-density non-LTE solutions would overshoot at S by 2.5-3.6x and are mildly (1.5-2 sigma) disfavoured, low-density ones undershoot. The data cannot separate the three at the +-30% error of the 254 line; none is needed to reproduce Harada.
results.uncertainty: +-30% on our 254 intensity at 1.7" (S: 0.69+-0.27 K km/s whole line) and +-10% (Harada, Table 13 errors) -> pred/Harada 0.84+-0.28 (S feathered), 0.69+-0.46 (N feathered); +-15% conversion (Trot 8-30 K); factor 0.9 (CMB contrast on/off, Q14k)

NON-LTE (q14k_radex.py, p-H2 collider of Rabli & Flower, Tbg 2.73 K, FWHM 150 km/s, equal E,A columns, beam filling 1): with I(254)=0.57 K km/s (S, Xb4f 6.3x3.8") the 254 line is sub-thermal (Tex 3-11 K, tau<0.1) and: R(254/Q-blend) at Tk=20 K = 9.6, 4.1, 0.70, 0.30, 0.20 for log n = 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7 (Tk 30-100 K within ~+-30% for n>=10^5); the observed 0.31 (0.22-0.37, q14c) needs n=10^5.5-10^6.5 cm-3 (any Tk 20-100 K); there R96/254 = 9-23 (vs 5-6 in LTE), R241/96 = 1.1-6.2, N_tot(A+E) = 10^14.26-10^14.70 = 1.8-5.0e14 cm-2 (thin: N = 3.2-8.8e14 per K km/s of 254; LTE 1.8, 2.7, 4.0e14 per K km/s at 10, 20, 30 K): non-LTE columns are 1.7-4.9x the LTE(10 K) and 0.8-2.2x the LTE(30 K) values; combined with Harada's S 241.79/96.74 = 0.70 the best (Tk,n) is Tk 20-24 K, n=10^5.2-10^5.5 (R96/254 = 23, N 10^14.5) but with chi2 8.9 (2 ratios; beams differ), at N n=10^6.1-7 (R96/254 7.5-12, N=10^13.7). Tex(CH3OH)~10-11 K from one thin-LTE pair is therefore a sub-thermal Tex (non-LTE), not Tk; Tk is unconstrained (20-100 K).

results.value: Rest frequencies (CDMS/JPL via out/splatalogue_raw.csv): 29SiO 8-7 342.98084 GHz (Eu 74 K, logA -2.67), 30SiO 6-5 254.21666 GHz (Eu 42.7 K, logA -3.07; NOT 254.76 as quoted in the review: the CH2NH 254.685/HC3N 254.70 feature is 570 km/s away); in sky frame 339.805 and 251.863 GHz. Template deblend (HCO+ profile; common v0, width): cluster 254: CH3OH (v0) + SiS 14-13 254.103 (+104 km/s) + 30SiO (+237 km/s); cluster 342.9: CS 7-6 + H2CS 10(0,10)-9(0,9) 342.946 (+56 km/s relative to CS) + 29SiO (+85 km/s; only 29 km/s from H2CS: correlation -0.8 to -0.95). RESULTS (K km/s, 6.3x3.8"; no detection): 30SiO 6-5 N -0.00+-0.06 (Xb4d) / -0.05+-0.09 (Xb4f), S +0.11+-0.07 / -0.11+-0.10, Bridge 0.03+-0.05 / -0.05+-0.10, Wclump 0.07+-0.06 / -0.09+-0.08, lobe 0.14+-0.07 / -0.04+-0.12 (3 sigma < 0.17-0.36); SiS 14-13 <0.15-0.3 (the 7 sigma 'SiS 14-13' in the Q0 table is CH3OH wing: with CH3OH+SiS+30SiO fitted jointly SiS is -0.14..+0.03+-0.05-0.1); 29SiO 8-7: joint (CS+H2CS+29SiO) N 0.08+-0.12, S -0.01+-0.16, Bridge 0.02+-0.16, lobe 0.16+-0.16 (3 sigma < 0.44, 0.47, 0.51, 0.65); with H2CS fixed to 0: N -0.02+-0.07, S -0.01+-0.07 (3 sigma < 0.20, 0.20, 0.16 Bridge, 0.29 lobe); CS 7-6 (deblended) N 1.13+-0.08, S 0.42+-0.10, Bridge 0.58+-0.10, W 0.31+-0.07, lobe 0.21+-0.10; H2CS 10(0,10) (29SiO=0) <0.23 (N), <0.25 (S) 3 sigma. COLUMNS (thin LTE, rigid rotor validated to 0.1% against LAMDA for CS 7-6, CMB contrast on): N(SiO)/N(CS) 3 sigma upper limits, 28Si/29Si=20 (15-30), 28Si/30Si=30 (25-35): from 29SiO (H2CS=0 / joint) at Tex 20 K: N 2.1 / 4.6, S 5.7 / 13.5, Bridge 3.3 / 10.6; at Tex 10-50 K: N 1.6-3.1 (H2CS=0) / 3.6-7.0 (joint), S 4.4-8.6 / 10.6-20; from 30SiO 6-5 (Xb4d) at Tex 10-50 K: N 0.33-2.1, S 1.6-10, Bridge 0.7-4.7. results.quantity: Q14h: summary: chemistry contrast between N, S, Bridge, S-outflow lobe and disk (what the data support)
results.value: (1) CH3OH is the only species with a region-dependent signal: extended (Xb4f flux rising to R=6"), compact peaks at the Bridge/W clump (1.0-1.2 K km/s at 1.7"), S-detected (4.6 sigma at 6.3x3.8") and N barely (1.2-1.6 sigma): S>N CH3OH/HCO+ = 0.022-0.025 vs 0.005-0.006 (S-N 2.8-3.0 sigma per array: MODERATE, not firm; <1.5 sigma at <=4.45"; the peaks sit 1-3" from both nuclei towards the Bridge/W clump); lobe 0.016-0.027, disk undetected (<0.017). Per H2 (dust, Td 30 K) X(CH3OH) = 1e-8-1e-7 at S/Bridge/W/lobe and (3-13)e-9 at N; S/N of X = 7.7 (4-19) at equal Tex, 1.9-2.4 for opposite Td/Tex differences: contrast not robust to T_N>T_S. (2) CS: N(CS)/N(H2) differs only 1.4x N/S (CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 uniform, 1.1+-0.2); SO, SiS, HCN v2=1 undetected; SiO: 29SiO/30SiO undetected but the limits are 5-360x above Harada's SiO/CS (0.06): untestable at this depth. (3) Harada+2018: with the matched whole-line estimator our 254 line predicts Harada's 96.74/HCO+ at 1.7" within ~1 sigma (pred/Harada 0.64-0.84 N,S in LTE at Harada's own Trot 11/17 K); the earlier 'x3 tension' was an estimator artefact; uv coverage, aperture/position and excitation are all allowed and none is required (Q14g). (4) CH3OH excitation: Tex(254) 5-7 K sub-thermal if n~1e5.5-1e6.5; N(CH3OH) 1.7-4.9x larger than LTE(10 K); Tk unconstrained. Ratios to HCO+ are not abundances: see Q14m for N(H2)- and H13CN-normalised proxies (all factor-3 uncertain). EXTERNAL INPUTS AND WHAT WAS NOT DONE: X(CH3OH) and X(CS) were NOT compared with the Harada+2018 fractional abundances (relative to H2/CO) - only the 96.74 GHz CH3OH/HCO+ intensities were compared (item 3); the dust N(H2) behind X assumes kappa(346 GHz)=0.02 cm2 per g gas (factor 2) and Td 20-50 K (factor 3.3); Harada+2018 (ApJ 855, 49) is used as an external assumption for its Table 1-3,13 setup/intensities.

results.quantity: Q13a: S-outflow blue-lobe HCN excess E = HCN-k*HCO+ (2375-2575 km/s) in Xb4d vs Xb4b at the SAME 1.05" beam, windows and apertures; reconciliation of 'Xb4d 6.2 sigma' with 'Xb4b 1 sigma'
results.value: [ROUND2] The 4.4 sigma (r=1") is a POINTWISE significance at a position selected on the same data; trials-corrected over the field it is 3.0-3.2 sigma (Q13g). Xb4d: E (Jy/beam km/s, mean in aperture, k=0.574) = 0.161+-0.044 (3.7 sigma, r=0.5"), 0.115+-0.026 (4.4 sigma, r=1.0"), 0.074+-0.017 (4.3 sigma, r=1.5"), 0.038+-0.013 (3.0 sigma, r=2.0"); 0 of 300 random apertures (r=0.5 and 1.0") reach E (p<0.003); the red mirror window (2975-3175) gives -0.062+-0.04 (r=0.5") and +0.019+-0.027 (r=1"): zero. Converted to flux 0.115 x 2.5 beams = 0.29 Jy km/s (r=1") reproduces team-b p0006-r02 E=0.262+-0.042 (k 0.534); our noise is 1.6x larger (random apertures include baseline/disk residual) so the same excess is 4.4 sigma here instead of 6.2 sigma: the difference is only the noise estimator. Xb4b (smoothed 1.05"): E = 0.107+-0.068 (1.6 sigma, r=0.5"), 0.035+-0.046 (0.8 sigma, 1"), 0.002+-0.031 (1.5"), -0.006+-0.026 (2"); 7-53 of 300 random apertures exceed it. If Xb4b recovered all of the Xb4d excess it would be detected at only 2.4, 2.5, 2.4, 1.5 sigma (Xb4b noise is 1.5-1.8x Xb4d at this beam), so the 'Xb4b 1 sigma' is a 1-2 sigma downward fluctuation or partial resolving-out, not a contradiction: recovery R=E(Xb4b)/E(Xb4d) = 0.67+-0.46 (0.5"), 0.31+-0.41 (1"), 0.02+-0.42 (1.5"), -0.16+-0.69 (2"); R=1 is disfavoured at 0.7, 1.7, 2.3, 1.7 sigma, i.e. no more than 2.3 sigma. Line recovery at the lobe (r=1"): HCN blue window 0.58+-0.22 (r=1.5": 0.37+-0.30), HCO+ blue 1.14+-0.49, HCN core 1.10+-0.34, HCO+ core 1.00+-0.33; at S 0.85+-0.11 (HCN), 0.92+-0.07 (HCO+), N 0.99+-0.03/0.99+-0.04, Bridge 0.82/0.86 (+-0.1). VERDICT: Xb4d and Xb4b are consistent (difference 0.7-2.0 sigma); the trend of R to smaller values with larger apertures is the signature expected for gas extended on >1" scales and partly filtered by the 0.25" configuration (consistent with the 55+-25% HCN recovery of Q3), but it is not demanded by the data; Xb4b cannot confirm or refute the excess.

results.value: (1) Blenders other than HDO: forward-modelled LTE ladders of CH3NH2, CH3OH, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH fitted to all other Band-6 channels at the lobe (Q3b, out/q3b/blend.log; c-C3H and l-C3H, HCN v2=1f and CH3CHO companions in team-b p0006-r02 s72c.txt): total blended fraction of the HCN flux <=0.10-0.18 in 2375-2575 (2 sigma envelope over T 15-120 K; <=0.42 at 2275-2375). (2) HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) 266.1611 GHz (Eu=157 K) is the only HDO line in the 250-266 GHz windows (catalogue dump: HDO 356.836 GHz, Eu 539 K, is the only other line in any band, undetectable); it lies -309.7 km/s from HCN, v_app = -309.7 + 1.00103 v_gas, i.e. gas at 2685-2885 km/s (the line core) would appear at 2375-2575: a blend is kinematically possible and has no second HDO line to test it. (3) Spectral test (22 km/s bins, 2100-2575 km/s; HDO template = HCO+ profile of the same aperture shifted by -309.7 km/s): residual HCN-k*HCO+ chi2 null/HDO-template/free-Gaussian wing/Gaussian+HDO = 68.8/34.5/20.4/20.3 (Xb4d r=0.5"; 27 bins) and 122.3/42.8/22.2/21.9 (r=1"); the HDO-with-gas-kinematics template is disfavoured against a free Gaussian (dchi2 14-21 for 2 extra parameters) and its share in the joint fit is -0.15+-0.38 (r=0.5") / -0.16+-0.30 (r=1") of E, i.e. <0.48 / <0.33 at 95%; Gaussian wing centre 2500-2506 km/s, sigma 93-117 km/s. In Xb4b the same fit is degenerate (HDO share 0.27+-0.28 / -0.19+-0.56). If the HDO line has arbitrary kinematics the spectrum alone allows 0-100%. (4) Chemical/spatial test: E in 2375-2575 per unit HCO+ emission of the parent-gas window (2685-2885): lobe 0.230 (E 4.9 sigma) vs 3 sigma limits S <0.027, N <0.014, Bridge <0.032, W clump <0.031 (E = 0.009+-0.024, 0.002, 0.013, -0.020 +-0.024 Jy/beam km/s there): a blend with an HDO/HCO+ ratio common to the regions is excluded; it requires a lobe-specific HDO enhancement of >=8.6x (S), >=16.9x (N), >=7.1x (Bridge), >=7.5x (W clump) relative to those regions (S nucleus: E <0.079 Jy/beam km/s at 3 sigma, 0.7x the lobe's 0.115 even though S has 6x more parent gas). SUMMARY OF THE BLEND-ALLOWED FRACTION of the HCN excess E: <=0.1-0.2 for all species except HDO; HDO with HCO+-like kinematics <0.33-0.48 (95%); HDO with arbitrary kinematics not constrained by the spectrum (<=1) but requiring a >=7-17x lobe-specific HDO enhancement. results.quantity: Q13f: SUMMARY: is the S-outflow blue-lobe HCN excess real dense wing gas? What survives, with blend-allowed fraction
results.value: [ROUND2] Qualification: E (HCN excess over k*HCO+) has pointwise 4.4 sigma but GLOBAL (post-selection) significance 3.0-3.2 sigma (blind search over the field, 141 independent apertures; Q13g), so it is MARGINAL (confidence medium-low); the lobe is an 8 sigma azimuthal outlier on the ring at the same distance from S (so S-nucleus residuals do not make it), HDO as the whole of E would need N(HDO)~1.5-2e15 cm-2 which is 20-2000x above any plausible HDO/H2 for the HCO+-implied N(H2) (Q13h; strongly disfavoured but not excluded, no second HDO line in the data). Text below predates this calibration; 'reproduced'/'real' in it mean pointwise. (1) Detection: the HCN blue-lobe excess E over k*HCO+ is reproduced in Xb4d at 4.4 sigma (r=1", 3.7-4.3 sigma for r=0.5-1.5") with a conservative empirical null (0/300 random apertures; team-b 6.2 sigma with a smaller noise estimate) and absent in the red mirror (+0.019+-0.027). HCO+ itself shows the blue wing at 4.2-5.2 sigma (Xb4d, 1.05"), independent of any HDO blend. (2) Xb4d vs Xb4b: consistent; Xb4b has 1.5-1.8x higher noise at 1.05" so even full recovery gives only 2.4-2.5 sigma (observed 0.8-1.6); R(E)=0.3-0.7+-0.4 at r<=1", falling to 0 at 1.5-2" (R=1 disfavoured <=2.3 sigma): the data neither require nor exclude partial resolving-out of extended (>1") excess. (3) Blend: all species other than HDO <=10-18% of E; HDO untestable by a companion line; with HCO+-like kinematics <33-48% (95%), any kinematics 0-100% but needing a lobe-specific >=7-17x HDO enhancement relative to S, N, Bridge, W clump; HCN 4-3 prediction test weakly favours real HCN (1.4 sigma). (4) What follows for the lobe: the dense-gas (HCO+, 4-5 sigma) blue lobe stands; its HCN/HCO+ is 1.3-1.8 (+-0.3-0.5) in the 2375-2575 window (2.2-3x the lobe-core 0.59), 0.74-0.76+-0.15 for the whole broad component, and 0.57 (=k) if E is entirely a blend: for a blended fraction f of E the E-window ratio is (HCN-f*E)/HCO+ = 1.78, 1.18, 0.58 for f=0, 0.5, 1 (Xb4d, r=1"). The HCN-based dense-gas mass of the lobe (Q3b: 1.4e6-4.6e6 Msun, route A) falls by up to a factor 2-3 for f=1 (E is 57-67% of the HCN blue-window flux); the HCO+-based mass (1.9e6-6.5e6) is unchanged. CLASSIFICATION: dense (HCO+/HCN) gas in the southern blue lobe: supported (medium); the elevated HCN/HCO+ (>1) in the blue wing: probable but not proven (medium-low: Xb4b cannot confirm, HDO cannot be excluded for arbitrary kinematics, 4-3 check weak). Decisive tests not possible here: a second HDO transition (e.g. 225.9 or 241.6 GHz, not in this data) or deeper HCN/HCO+ 4-3 at <=1".
results.uncertainty: E 4.4 sigma pointwise, 3.0-3.2 sigma global (Xb4d); blend fraction see Q13c; ratio see Q13b

results.quantity: Q13g: global (post-selection) significance of the S-lobe HCN excess E and matched-environment (ring) null
results.value: POST-SELECTION CALIBRATION (Q13g): the 4.4 sigma is a POINTWISE value at a position chosen as the HCN blue-lobe peak. Blind search of the Xb4d E map (E=HCN-0.574*HCO+, 2375-2575 km/s, 1.05" beam, r=1" disk mean, field r<=7.5", 141 independent 1" apertures): the lobe (E=0.116 at (-0.2,-4.7)") is the highest of 12 local maxima (next 0.075 at (-4.7,+3.4)", 0.064 at (2.4,1.9)"; the rank alone is p=1/12); with the E-map robust sigma 0.0264 (includes real structure) z=4.40, p_local=5.4e-6, trials-corrected p_global=7.6e-4 = 3.2 sigma one-sided (3.0 sigma with the random-aperture sigma 0.027). The red mirror window peaks at 0.156 (0.134 at (-4.7,+3.4)", 0.098 at (-5.3,-2.9)") with map sigma 0.040, i.e. the field has red-side E maxima of 2.9 sigma local (global 0.8 sigma) so the E noise is not purely Gaussian. Sliding 200 km/s line-free windows (HCN 1380-2100 and HCO+ free ranges) give far lower noise (sigma 0.008, max E over the field 0.020-0.027, none near 0.116) but those channels are far from the line and miss the wing/sidelobe/baseline structure of the line window, so they are NOT used for the significance (only as a statement that no instrumental E of this size occurs in emission-free channels). Matched environment (ring of r=1.93" around S through the lobe, 10-deg steps, E window): excluding the lobe azimuth +-45 deg the ring has mean 0.000, sd 0.015, max 0.031 (lobe is +8.0 sigma of the ring, and the only ring point >0.031); the same ring in the red mirror window has sd 0.039 and max 0.091 (lobe 2.4 sigma above it); the ring around N: blue sd 0.025 max 0.056, red max 0.143. (The reviewer's '4.5" from S' is the lobe distance from the phase centre; the lobe is 1.93" = 0.38 kpc S of S.) Result: GLOBAL significance 3.0-3.2 sigma (one-sided), below the 4 sigma bar: E is MARGINAL as a standalone detection of excess HCN over k*HCO+; HDO cannot be excluded and the (separately detected) HCO+ blue wing is the secure part. Caveat: the trials factor assumes the lobe position would have been searched over the whole field (conservative; if the S side 3.5-5.5" annulus only is searched N_ind~45 and p_global~2.4e-4 = 3.5 sigma).
results.uncertainty: global 3.0-3.2 sigma (one-sided); depends on N_ind (141 field; ~45 for the S annulus) and on the Gaussian tail assumption

results.quantity: Q13h: LTE column of HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) required if the whole lobe excess E were HDO, vs plausible HDO/H2
results.value: E=0.115+-0.027 Jy/beam km/s in the 1.05" beam = 1.80+-0.42 K km/s (beam-filling) at 266.161 GHz (Eu=157.2 K, A=1.75e-5 s-1, g_u=5, Q(T)=588*(T/300)^1.5; thin LTE, CMB corrected). Required N(HDO) = 2.6e15 (50 K), 1.5e15 (100 K), 1.7e15 (150 K), 2.0e15 (200 K), 2.8e15 (300 K) cm-2 (+-25%), larger by (1.05"/size)^2 if the emitter is smaller than the beam. The parent gas (HCO+ 2685-2885 at the same aperture, 7.8 K km/s) has thin-LTE N(HCO+) = 0.65-1.1e13 (100-200 K), so HDO/HCO+ would have to be 170-240 (a lower limit on N(HCO+) only if HCO+ is thin; thick HCO+ raises it by a few). With X(HCO+)=1e-9..1e-8: N(H2)=0.7-11e21 and HDO/H2 = 1.7e-7..2.4e-6 (T 100-300 K) - i.e. 17-1000x above the reviewer's 1e-9-1e-8 and at/above the highest Galactic hot-core/hot-corino values (~1e-7). Forward: for X(HDO)=1e-9..1e-8 and N(H2) from HCO+ the HDO line would be 0.06-6 mJy/beam km/s versus the observed E = 115, i.e. 20-2000x too weak. Independent check from mass: the Q3b dense mass 1.4e6-6.5e6 Msun over the 3x2.7" box gives <N(H2)>~1e21 cm-2, needing HDO/H2~2e-6 (and gas at 100-300 K over ~0.5 kpc, which the HCN/HCO+ ladder (Q12: Tkin 16-40 K) does not support). VERDICT: E as HDO is strongly disfavoured chemically/energetically; not excluded observationally (no second HDO line, HDO/H2 of the lobe is unmeasured).

results.quantity: Q15a: red-shifted HCN 3-2 ridge ~3.3" N of S: flux, significance, baseline systematics (Xb4d, 1.05")
results.value: Red wing +230..+470 km/s at the ridge: 0.126+-0.022 Jy/beam km/s (stat; scatter of 400 random r=1" apertures in the same window map, which is 3x the line-free-window noise 0.0075 because of baseline extrapolation and real disk structure) = 5.9 sigma pointwise. Baseline systematic: the Q3 free channels are all BLUE of the line (HCN 1380-2100), so the red side is an extrapolation; ridge flux is 0.098 (order 0), 0.207 (order 1, blue only), 0.126 (blue + red edge >3290 km/s, order 1), 0.138 (order 2 with edge): so +-0.05 systematic (sigma_tot ~0.055 -> 2.3 sigma if one takes the extremes at face value, but all variants are positive and the control apertures (3.5,-1.5), (-3,-6) stay at -0.01..+0.01 in the edge-anchored baselines). Baseline-FREE cross-check: the Xb4d tapered cube (30 km/s channels, covers 2351-3214 km/s, flat controls) gives 0.093 Jy/b km/s at the ridge versus control scatter ~0.01 (4 control apertures: -0.010, +0.006, -0.010, +0.008). The blue mirror at the ridge is -0.002 (no blue wing there), and the ridge red wing is 1 of the brightest maxima of the red map. results.quantity: Q15h: SUMMARY - is the red ridge real, and is it an S counter-lobe, Bridge streaming gas, or N-related? Is the S outflow bipolar in dense gas?
results.value: (1) REAL: yes in HCN (5.9 sigma pointwise at an a-priori position, recovered in Xb4b at 0.84+-0.22 of Xb4d, in the baseline-free tapered cube, absent as a blue wing, ~2x the N-wing level and 1.7" away from N so not N beam leakage); only tentative in HCO+ (2-4 sigma); 4-3 gives no constraint. Flux scale +-40% from the red-side baseline. (2) ORIGIN: UNDECIDED. Counter-lobe of S: favoured by (a) coincidence with M18 OF-Red (0.6-0.7"), (b) near-symmetric wing velocities (+290/-262 km/s) and flux (1.2+-0.3), (c) both wings detached from S by ~2" on the same axis. Against: ridge distance 646 pc vs 375 pc, and the red wing does not end at the ridge but continues, weaker, to N. Bridge-streaming / N-related: favoured by (a) the ridge core gas moves with N/Bridge (2780-2793 km/s, +40 from S) while the lobe core is -30 from S, (b) the continuous red tongue N->S peaking 1.8" S of N and N's own red-only wing; against: the +260 km/s wing velocity relative to local gas is ~9x the N-S core-centroid difference (29 km/s) and needs a >250 km/s non-circular flow over 350-650 pc (not excluded in a coalescing pair), and the N HCN pole-on/blue limits (Q3b). HCN/HCO+ (3.3+-1.8 vs 2.0+-0.7) cannot separate them. Needed: CO or HCN/HCO+ at 1-0/2-1 wings at <=1" with p-v along the axis (not in this archive). (3) BIPOLAR: dense-gas bipolarity of the S outflow is PERMITTED but NOT ESTABLISHED: if the ridge is the counter-lobe, total dense outflow mass x1.7-2.2 (Q15f); otherwise the S dense outflow is one-sided (blue lobe only, itself marginal as an excess over k*HCO+ at 3.2 sigma global, Q13g; the HCO+ blue wing 4-5 sigma is the secure part). Do not combine the ridge into the S mass-outflow budget until the origin is decided.
results.uncertainty: ridge detection medium (HCN), tentative (HCO+); origin undecided

results.quantity: Q5a: is the 0.25" sub-structure of N, S and the Bridge real, and how many sub-clumps does N split into?
results.value: Thermal noise of the +-350 km/s moment-0 map is 0.008-0.015 Jy/b km/s (line-free sums, 0 local maxima >0.1 in the null maps) but the window map has pixel scatter 0.12-0.14 (MAD, |r|<5.5") from real structure (clumpy emission plus sparse uv sampling), so S/N maps of 20-60 overstate clump significance. The 1"-high-pass maps of the two lines correlate at lag 0 with r=0.74 (N, r<2.2"), 0.60 (S), 0.68 (Bridge), 0.49 (whole r<5.5"), i.e. 5.3, 4.9, 4.0 and 7.8 sigma against 300 random shifts of the HCO+ map: the sub-structure is shared by both lines and therefore real. Matched local maxima (HCN and HCO+ within 0.2", high-pass >0.15 Jy/b km/s): 8 in r<5.5" (N 3, S 4, Bridge 1) with 1.7+-1.2 expected by chance (null: HCO+ map shifted 1-2.5"); at >0.2: 3 matched, 0.2+-0.5 by chance. The earlier statement 'N splits into >=5 sub-clumps' is NOT reproduced as a significant count: N has a bright core (-0.05,+2.63)" (HCN 1.0, HCO+ 0.94 Jy/b km/s smoothed) plus 2-3 weaker matched clumps ((-0.5,+1.9), (+1.26,+2.11), and (+1.12,+1.3) towards the Bridge), the rest of the >5-sub-clump list is at chance level. Clump morphology: N = bright 0.3-0.6" core inside a ~1.5" x 0.35" (290x70 pc) ridge elongated at PA ~112 deg (both lines) with a ~1" envelope; S = compact core with E-W extension; Bridge = arc 1.5" long at PA ~50 deg. Null caveat (round 2): the shifts (1-2.5", i.e. 4-10 beams) remove the beam-correlated signal but not the extended real structure of the shifted map, so the shifted-map null is only a test of coincidence, not of clump significance; the per-line sizes are therefore treated with the radius-dependence systematics of Q5b.

results.quantity: Q5h: HCN vs HCO+ size of the N and S cores at matched resolution, the HCN/HCO+ ratio profile, and reconciliation with team-b p0005/p0007 and team-a p0005-r02
results.value: Gaussian-fit sizes cannot separate the two lines: N core HCN 0.20-0.47" (major 0.24-0.70") vs HCO+ 0.26-0.29" (major 0.53-0.62", minor 0.12-0.15") over fit radii 0.3-0.6": the ranges overlap, so the round-1 'HCN 0.72x0.31 vs HCO+ 0.61x0.12 at N' is not a >3 sigma size difference (the noise-only injection error is 0.01-0.03", the radius/model systematics are 0.1-0.25"); S core HCN is unconstrained (<~0.6"). MODEL-INDEPENDENT test (both cubes' +-350 km/s moment-0 maps convolved to a common 0.30" circular beam, profiles about the HCO+ peak, background from r=1.5-2" or 1-1.5" or none): half-light radius r50(HCN)-r50(HCO+) = -0.06 (N; -0.01..-0.06 over the background choice) and -0.07 (S; -0.04..-0.08) arcsec, noise sd 0.002-0.010"; r50 N 0.50 vs 0.56" (97 vs 109 pc), S 0.37 vs 0.44" (72 vs 86 pc); r75 N 0.69 vs 0.75", S 0.59 vs 0.69". So HCN is equal to or up to ~15% MORE COMPACT than HCO+ at both nuclei (HCN/HCO+ r50 ratio 0.89-0.98 N, 0.85-0.90 S); the round-1 statement 'HCN is 1.2-1.8x larger than HCO+' is withdrawn (it came from unstable single-Gaussian fits of HCN at larger fit radii). HCN/HCO+ moment-0 ratio profile at 0.30" (annuli 0-0.1/0.1-0.2/0.2-0.3/0.3-0.45/0.45-0.6/0.6-0.8/0.8-1.0/1.0-1.5"): N 1.01/0.99/0.97/0.93/0.80/0.73/0.67/0.37 (+-0.01-0.015); S 0.37/0.35/0.37/0.40/0.26/0.24/0.26/0.19 (+-0.01-0.02). RECONCILIATION: (i) agrees with team-b p0005 (N 0.97/0.87/0.65/0.41 for <0.25/0.25-0.5/0.5-1/1-2" at 0.25") and team-a p0005-r02 (0.98/0.95/0.87/0.64/0.45 at 0.30"): the N core has ratio ~1.0 inside r~0.3" (<=60 pc) and falls to 0.4 by 1-1.5"; this is a radial profile difference (HCN falls faster outward than HCO+), not a larger HCN size; r02's 'resolved ~0.6" (FWHM) excess' is the 0.3-0.6" shoulder of this profile. (ii) S is flat at 0.35-0.40 inside 0.45" and drops to ~0.25 outside (p0005: flat 0.37-0.43 to 3" at 0.94"/blended beams; consistent at 0.25" inside 0.45", slightly lower beyond). (iii) p0007's width null (HCN/HCO+ FWHM 1.085+-0.015 in 0.30" r<0.25") is consistent with equal-size, equal-width cores and our intrinsic sigma ratio 1.1-1.25 at R<=0.25" (1-2 sigma). Consequence for Q1/Q2 beam filling: a common filling factor for HCN and HCO+ (equal within ~15%, HCN not larger) is supported at the N and S cores at 0.25-0.3" resolution; the ratio gradient is carried by the excitation/opacity/abundance profile, not by different filling. At the S core the HCN/HCO+ ratio of 0.37 at equal size means the S deficit is in brightness temperature, not geometric dilution.
results.uncertainty: r50 differences +-0.01" (noise), +-0.03" (background choice); ratio +-0.01-0.02 per annulus

results.value: (1) Sizes: only the N-core HCO+ (0.26-0.29", 50-56 pc; a ridge 100-120 x 23-30 pc), S-core HCO+ (0.25-0.34", 49-66 pc) and a clump 1.2" E of S in HCN (0.31-0.35") have stable deconvolved sizes (<= 1.5 beam, geometric FWHM); N-core HCN is 0.20-0.47" (range), everything else is an upper limit or unconstrained. The injection test shows a noise-limited size error of 0.01-0.06"; the radius-dependence of the real (non-Gaussian) structure is the true error. (2) HCN is not larger than HCO+: matched-beam half-light radii are 0.50 vs 0.56" (N) and 0.37 vs 0.44" (S); ratio ~1.0 inside r~0.3" at N, 0.37 flat at S; common filling is supported (round-1 'HCN 1.2-1.8x larger' withdrawn). (3) Offsets: lines and 1.1 mm continuum coincide to <=0.10" (20 pc, 0.4 beam) at N and <=0.05" (10 pc, 0.2 beam) at S; thermal positional errors are <=0.01"; measured displacements (S HCO+ 0.03-0.05" S of the continuum; N HCO+ 0.07-0.10" E; N HCN-HCO+ peaks 0.05-0.09") are 0.1-0.4 beam, inseparable from structure/astrometric systematics; Bridge undefined. (4) Kinematics: N is a flat rotation curve (Vlos 65+-3 km/s, kinematic PA 80+-2 deg, Rt<=0.2"), S is only roughly described by an E-W rotator (HCO+: PA 110+-4 deg, Vlos 78+-5; chi2_red 13.6; HCN not fitted) and its gradient at R<0.4" is unconstrained (69+-59 km/s/" in HCN, 1.2 sigma). (5) Beam smearing explains 24-25 of the 55-70 km/s peak-pixel dispersion at N and ~16 of ~50 at S; intrinsic sigma is centrally peaked at N (63-79 at R~0 to 24 km/s at 1"); one-beam intrinsic sigma N 50 (HCO+) - 66 (HCN), S 47-50 km/s. results.quantity: Q20c: p0028 'Tk lower limit survives free eta' is SUPPORTED at P(T>50 K)=0.6-0.9 for realistic correlated errors (not 'confirmed'); the quoted dchi2 36-41 against 25 K is not reproduced (5-15)
results.value: Error model (scripts/q20f_10arcsec_corr.py): per-line independent error = 3% stat (+) aperture/beam-matching (2-1: 10%, as the 9.4x6.2" B5 beam is comparable to the 10" aperture and loses extended flux; 3-2: 3%; 4-3: 5%), plus a common per-band flux-scale factor (B5, B6, B7; Gaussian 10% in ln, shared by HCN and HCO+, marginalised analytically via the covariance). ALMA B5-B7 absolute flux accuracy is ~10% per band, hence sigma_g=10%; the 7% case is dropped. Results (p0028 intensities; shared eta / separate eta; Tbg 2.73 K -> Tbg 5 K): baseline (sigma_g 10%, aperture x1): N T=100 [80,134] / 92 [52,128] K, P(T>50)=0.93/0.85 (Tbg 5: 0.79/0.77), P(T<=30)=0.05/0.07 (0.11/0.08); S T=79 [57,93] / 81 [58,94] K, P(T>50)=0.90/0.91 (0.87/0.83), P(T<=30)=0.06/0.04 (0.09/0.05). Aperture error x2: P(T>50)=0.71-0.77 (Tbg 2.73), 0.63-0.66 (Tbg 5); P(T<=30)=0.11-0.16 (0.13-0.21). sigma_g=15%: P(T>50)=0.75-0.83 (0.64-0.76). Old uncorrelated 15% (reference): 0.71-0.78 (0.57-0.67). So the warm 10" solution is supported at P(T>50)=0.6-0.9, P(T<=30)=0.04-0.2, depending on Tbg and the aperture error, with eta_med 0.05-0.1 (area factor of the 10" aperture, tau32(HCN) 24-80 = very thick). Cold-gas test (eta>=0.05, T=25 K): dchi2 relative to best = 5.7 (S sep) to 15 (S shared), 4.4 (N sep) to 9.6 (N shared) at baseline errors, versus 36-41 quoted by p0028: p0028's cold-gas exclusion is therefore NOT reproduced as a >5 sigma result; it is a 2-4 sigma preference. Verdict: Tk lower limit of ~50 K at 10": supported (probability 0.6-0.9), REVISED in strength. It constrains the envelope: the core share of the 10" 3-2 flux is 4-11% (Gaussian core) to 10-28% (pedestal-inclusive) (Q20e).

results.quantity: Q11b: forward model of recovery (sky x primary beam -> uv transfer function T(u) -> /PB -> 10" beam) using the Xb55 2-1 10" maps as proxy sky: what intrinsic extra HCN/HCO+ fall at r>=10" does the 3-2 need?
results.value: With T(u)=clip((u-ua)/ua,0,1), ua=f*8.7m/lambda: the observed 3-2 HCO+ profile (fluxes 26.6/44.2/16.1 Jy km/s at 0-4/4-8/8-12", equal to 2-1 to 5% at r<8") needs f=0.075-0.275 (ua=0.6-2.1 kl; fuller recovery than a hard 8.7 m cut, which would remove 70-100% of the flux at r<8"; a hard cut at ua>=3.9 kl is excluded because it makes the 8-12" flux negative). Imposing no extra gradient (proxy truth = 2-1) a 3-2 observation would give R(8-12")/R(0-4") = 0.80-0.84 (2-1 truth: 0.85) at f=0.1-0.2, i.e. recovery by itself does not produce the observed 0.44 (3-2: 0.193/0.442). Fitting the extra intrinsic HCN fall eps (ramp 0 at 4" -> eps at >=10") to the 3-2 ratios 0-4/4-8/8-12": Xb4f eps=0.15 (1 sigma 0.10-0.20; 2 sigma 0.05-0.25) f free; eps=0.20 (0.15-0.20) with f tied to the HCO+ flux profile; Xb4d eps=0.35 (0.25-0.40; 2 sigma 0.20-0.45), 0.30 with f tied. So the 3-2 intrinsic HCN/HCO+ falls MORE with radius than the 2-1 by ~15-35% (extra, relative) at 8-12", total true 3-2 R(10")/R(<=4") ~0.55-0.75 versus 0.85 for 2-1. The 2-1 decline of 11% itself is a mild effect of the proxy: it is the data, so unchanged. A flat intrinsic HCN/HCO+ (eps=0) is excluded at >2 sigma in all 6 fits but only for the assumed sigma on the 8-12" ratio (0.06) and given the PB/T(u) parameterisation [Q25 note: the 2-1 8-12/4-8 decline (11%) is an upper bound: adding back the maximal uniform bowl estimated from the cumulative flux (16-30") gives 0.914 (decline 8.6%); the 22-35" ring-mean offset gives 0.895 (10.5%); the same bowl-like negative pattern is present in the Michiyama 1-0 (6-10%). See Q25.]
results.uncertainty: eps +-0.10 (Xb4f) / +-0.07 (Xb4d) statistical-in-fit; model systematics (T(u) shape, PB width 22 vs 37", zero level, 8-12" sigma assumed 0.06) not marginalised: treat eps as 0.05-0.45

results.quantity: Q11d: summary and physical consequence: is there a genuine disk gradient in HCN/HCO+ beyond nuclear weighting?
results.value: (1) 2-1: 8-12" ratio is 7-18% below the 4-8" one depending on the beam (0.492 in 10" circ), reproduced from team-b s36 (0.49+-0.03; 0.575/0.554/0.489). Flat intrinsic HCN/HCO+ is not excluded by the 2-1 data alone: the forward model gives chi2 4.2 (eps=-0.1) to 1.1 (eps=0.4) for a 5%+1 Jy km/s flux error floor, i.e. the 2-1 gradient is unconstrained to eps=0-0.4. (2) 3-2: the 8-12" annulus ratio is unmeasurable directly, but with the recovery calibrated on the HCO+ profile the 3-2 requires an extra intrinsic fall eps=0.05-0.45 (best 0.15-0.35) beyond the 2-1; the 2-1 vs 3-2 difference is therefore an excitation/density-temperature effect that the 3-2 is more sensitive to (HCN 3-2/2-1 line ratio drops 0.76 at r<8" to 0.27 at 8-12" in Jy km/s, HCO+ drops 1.0 -> 0.70; Tb ratio r32/21=0.34 -> 0.12 for HCN, 0.45 -> 0.31 for HCO+; part of the HCO+ drop is degenerate with recovery). (3) RADEX ladder grids (LAMDA, dv=150, out/q1): a 15% lower R21 alone is a change of log X=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) of only about -0.07 dex if optically thin; the stronger 3-2 fall (q=R32(8-12)/R32(inner)=0.58-0.77) cannot be made by abundance: it requires lower excitation of HCN relative to HCO+ in the outer disk, the grid matches (7% tolerance, 0.25 dex steps) exist for fixed Tk=20-50 K with the outer zone at a lower N(HCN)/N(HCO+) by up to ~0.5 dex or at lower density; non-unique, not constrained further. (4) Not a gradient in the abundance ratio is required; the 3-2/2-1 ladder change is in the excitation. What would settle it: 3-2 and 2-1 (and 1-0) with the same uv coverage plus total power (the raw data are available: re-imaging with a common uv range, 7-m only, would remove the recovery degeneracy) [Q25 note: the 2-1 8-12/4-8 decline (11%) is an upper bound: adding back the maximal uniform bowl estimated from the cumulative flux (16-30") gives 0.914 (decline 8.6%); the 22-35" ring-mean offset gives 0.895 (10.5%); the same bowl-like negative pattern is present in the Michiyama 1-0 (6-10%). See Q25.]
results.uncertainty: see Q11a-c; eps 0.05-0.45; RADEX translation is a non-unique 2-zone match with 7% tolerance, 0.25 dex grid

results.quantity: Q25a: HCN/HCO+ 1-0 disk ratio at 10" beam, annuli 0-4/4-8/6-9/8-12": Michiyama 0.645/0.619/0.602/0.559 (no zero-level correction; 0.650/0.628/0.615/0.589 with maximal bowl add-back), Harada 0.648/0.610/0.576/0.447 (recovery-limited, not trusted at 8-12")
results.value: [round2 systematics] 8-12/4-8 decline factor, Michiyama 1-0: 0.902 (no correction) to 0.937 (maximal uniform bowl add-back = -mean of the 22-35" ring: -0.59 HCN, -0.73 HCO+ Jy/beam km/s) => decline 6-10% (not 10+-1.6%). Window +-250/350/500 km/s changes it by <0.001 (0.902/0.902/0.901). Per-channel (annulus spectra): the bowl exists only at line velocities (-2 to -3 mJy/beam at 10" vs +14-16 mJy HCN and 25-28 mJy HCO+ in the 8-12" ring), the line-free windows have mean offset <0.1 Jy/beam km/s (rms 0.05): the bowl is a line-proportional negative, as expected from missing short spacings, so a constant add-back is an upper bound on the correction only if there is no real emission at 22-35" (otherwise the true bowl is larger). Harada: 0.733 (to 0.78 with add-back; window-dependent 0.76/0.73/0.66 for +-250/350/500, ring std 1.8-2.5, i.e. unreliable) - rejected at 8-12". uv properties: only images are available (no visibilities restored, MRS not in the headers); both 1-0 sets are 12m-only Cycle-3 (2.1" and 1.4" beams), minimum baseline ~15m (4.4 kl) => MRS ~10-30" depending on configuration (not measured); Fourier ratio Harada/Michiyama of the 10" maps is 0.6-0.7 at 1-4 kl and >1.3 above 4 kl (log q25_growth.log), i.e. Harada under-represents the 50-200" scales (and over-weights small scales in the normalisation); the Harada cumulative flux is 0.75-0.78 of that of Michiyama inside 12" and 0.5-0.57 inside 20". Michiyama is preferred because Xb55 and Michiyama both pass the high-pass 0.5-3 kl test with a stable 8-12/4-8 factor (0.90-0.92, 0.89-0.86), not because it has more flux; neither dataset is complete (cumulative flux falls beyond 16" in both). Literature: Harada+2018 give per-nucleus 1-0 ratios only; no disk ring value published.
results.uncertainty: statistical +-0.016 on the factor; zero-level systematic +0.00/+0.035 (dominant, 2x the statistic); 8-12" Harada recovery-limited

results.quantity: Q25c: RADEX translation of the 1-0/2-1 disk ratios (Michiyama 1-0 + Xb55 2-1, 10"): no HCN/HCO+ abundance gradient is required; a modest density drop in the outer annulus suffices (low confidence)
results.value: [round2 systematics] Softened: the RADEX statement stands only at its resolution. The ring-to-ring R21/R10 is flat within +-5% under all zero-level scenarios; a 5% change in R21 corresponds to ~0.02 dex in log X (earlier estimate: 15% -> ~0.07 dex) and far less than the 0.25 dex grid step, so the fit result (log X = +0.50 constant, delta log X=0.00 +-0.25; allowed outer density decrease 0-0.5 dex) is unchanged; the fit was not re-run per scenario. No abundance gradient and no excitation change is REQUIRED by the 1-0/2-1 data; a 0-0.5 dex lower n at 8-12" is allowed. Chi2 fit of [R10, R21, HCN 2-1/1-0, HCO+ 2-1/1-0] on the LAMDA RADEX grid (Tk 10-150 K, log n 3-8, N 1e13-3e18, dv 150 km/s, Tbg 2.73 K; errors 4% ratios, 14% ladders; scripts/q25_radexfit.py, out/q25/q25_radexfit.log). X=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) is pinned at log X=+0.50 (3.2) in all annuli (0-4, 4-8, 8-12") for Tk=20-50 K, i.e. delta log X = 0.00 (+-0.25 grid step): no abundance-ratio gradient needed. At Tk=20 K log n 4.75-5.00 (4-8") -> 4.25-4.75 (8-12"); Tk=30-50 K log n 3-5.0 -> 3-4.75/4.5: a ~0.25-0.5 dex density decrease is allowed/preferred but not required (degenerate with N, which is poorly bounded: log N(HCO+) 15.5-17.75). Fits at fixed Tk have chi2 3-10 for 0 dof-ish (4 obs, 3 free: logn, NH, NO), i.e. acceptable. Same fit to Harada: 8-12" demands log n 6.25 and log X<-0.75 (unphysical ladders ~1), rejecting Harada's 8-12" flux as incomplete. Caveat: single-zone, same dv/beam filling for all lines, no hyperfine HCN, LAMDA collision rates with H2 only.
results.uncertainty: grid step 0.25 dex; degenerate N-n-Tk

results.quantity: Q10g: RADEX consequences (LAMDA, Tbg 2.73 K, dv 150 km/s): what each interpretation predicts for R vs continuum and for the ladders
results.target: N and S, grid Tk 20-150 K, log n 3-7, N(HCO+) 1e14-1e17, X 0.3-30
results.value: R32 (Tb ratio) saturates at ~1 for thick, thermalised gas (e.g. Tk=30, N(HCO+)=1e16.5, n>=1e6: R=0.82-1.0 even for X=3), so the N core R=0.93-1.0 sits at the ceiling; it cannot rise further with continuum. Reference S-like state (Tk 30-80, log n=4, N(HCO+)=1e16, X=3): R=0.29-0.40. Single-parameter moves to R~1.0: (i) abundance ratio X x3-4 (X 3->10): R=0.97-1.22 with 4-3/3-2 unchanged (HCN 0.23-0.39, HCO+ 0.35-0.47) -- matches the observed similar N/S ladders (HCN 0.39/0.27, HCO+ 0.48/0.44); (ii) density 1e4->1e6.5: R=0.4->0.8-1.0 but HCN 4-3/3-2 -> 0.78-0.9 (excluded by 0.39); (iii) column N(HCO+) 1e16->1e17: R only 0.29->0.43 (Tk=30), 0.40->0.52 (80 K); (iv) IR pumping/Tbg: dust Tb at 355 GHz 0.3 (N)/1.0 K (S) -> Tbg,eff 3.0/3.7 K, R changes <few %, v2=1f <3-6%. => abundance (X(HCN)/X(HCO+) up by ~0.5-0.6 dex, equivalently HCO+ depleted/destroyed in N) is the only single change that explains R without changing ladders; HCN and HCO+ individually: HCO+ ∝ continuum, HCN concentrates (Q10a). With CS 7-6/HCO+ N/S = 2.1+-0.3 but CS/HCN 1.1+-0.2 (Q14e, 4-6" beams) N is HCO+-poor rather than HCN-rich relative to S. Not discriminated: starburst chemistry (mechanical heating/cosmic rays: would make R follow SFR density, which is not seen across nuclei), XDR/AGN (S has the AGN, but lowest R, so an X-ray/AGN-driven HCN enhancement is disfavoured at S); HCO+ destruction by higher electron fraction/lower ionisation in the dense N core is allowed.
results.uncertainty: grid steps 0.5 dex in n, 1 dex in N; ladders from Q1b
