results.quantity: Q23g (replaces Q23c): conditional Tk lower limits from CO(2-1) and the beam-dilution fit
results.value: Assuming CO(2-1) thick with Tex<=Tk and T_b = ff[J(Tex)-J(2.73)](1-e^-tau): at 0.26" with ff=1, tau>=3: S Tk>=38 K (peak channel, 31.2 RJ) or >=26 K (mean over the HCN FWHM, 20.1 RJ); N >=19 K (peak) or >=17 K (HCN-mean). For ff=0.5: S 71/48 K, N 34/30; ff=0.3: S 115/76, N 52/46; ff=0.2: S 170/111, N 76/66 (tau=3; tau=1 values +40-50%). Beam dilution: a Gaussian source of FWHM theta fitted to T_b(beam) over 0.18-1.7": S theta=0.71+-0.08" (150 pc), Ts=33.9+-2.3 K peak (21.7+-1.4 HCN-mean) giving ff=0.88/0.61/0.15 at 0.26/0.57/1.7"; N theta=1.1-1.3+-0.3", Ts=13.4+-1.7 (11.6+-1.1), ff=0.95/0.79/0.3. So at 0.26" the CO core is ~unresolved-to-filled (ff 0.9) for the tau>=3 case and the HCN-velocity-matched S lower limit Tk>=26 K is only marginally above the 17-25 K S RADEX core; the peak-channel limit Tk>=38 K is in tension with 17-25 K only if the HCN gas fills the CO-bright 0.26" core at that velocity. Conditional statement: S cannot be a 17-25 K space-filling core if CO is thick, co-spatial and 12m flux is complete (a 5-10% missing flux raises the limits); it can be if CO(2-1) is sub-thermal/partly thin (tau(CO)~1 lowers Tex, not raising Tk_min above the table at tau>=3 but the tau=1 row gives the larger limits), or if HCN/HCO+ is cooler layer/clump along the line of sight. 13CO/C18O(2-1) is not available at this resolution, so tau(CO) is not constrained; velocity mismatch, co-spatiality and CO-vs-HCN beam dilution are unmodelled. Use as Q22 prior: Tk(S) lower bound 26-38 K at 0.26" for ff~1, tau>=3 (>=70 K for ff~0.5); N >=17-19 K.
results.uncertainty: fit uncertainties theta +-0.08" (S), +-0.3" (N); Tk_min +-15% from T_b systematics (position, flux)

results.quantity: Q32a: 0.26" vs 1.0" 12CO(2-1) flux at matched uv, and is the compact component resolved?
results.value: Flux in the beam (T_b*theta^2, same 12m cube, same uv coverage): the 0.26" beam recovers 0.18 (S) and 0.12 (N) of the 1.0"-beam peak flux (peak channel; 3-ch 0.18/0.12; HCN window 0.17/0.11), i.e. T_b rises only x2.7 (S) and x1.8 (N) from 1.0" to 0.26" where a point source would give x14.8 and a source filling 1" x1. Both cores are therefore resolved at 0.18" (T_b: S 34.8, 30.4, 24.8, 18.7, 14.9, 11.4, 6.5 K RJ for beams native 0.18, 0.26, 0.38, 0.57, 0.75, 1.0, 1.7"; N 15.6, 13.2, 10.3, 8.3, 7.7, 7.3, 5.9 K); this is model-independent. The size and ff depend on the profile model. S, peak channel, deconvolved FWHM s / ff(0.26") / core T0 (K RJ): Gauss+pedestal 0.52 (0.48-0.56)" / 0.80 (0.77-0.82) / 33.5; Gauss+free-size extended 0.38 (0.27-0.48)" / 0.68 (0.51-0.77) / 29; exponential+pedestal 0.35" / 0.60 / 47; Moffat+pedestal 0.48" / 0.77 / 36; single Gaussian 0.71" / 0.88 / 33.6 (chi2 11.6/5, disfavoured but errors are loose); direct 2D fit with clumps modelled s=0.38-0.57" (0.38-0.43" with 3 clumps), ff(0.26")=0.68-0.83, T0=30-33 K. Envelope S: s=0.35-0.71" (75-150 pc), ff(0.26")=0.60-0.89 (best-supported 0.68-0.80), ff(0.18")=0.70-0.94. The same fits to the 3-ch mean and HCN-window mean give the same s and ff within 0.02 (S window T0=21-25 K). N, peak channel: Gauss+pedestal s=0.27" / ff 0.52 / T0 13.8 K; free-size ext 0.21" / 0.40 / 15; exponential 0.14" / 0.32 / 22; Moffat 0.23" / 0.46 / 16; single Gaussian rejected (chi2 32/5, s=1.2"); 2D fits s=0.18-0.24", ff(0.26")=0.33-0.45 (unstable, 0.11-0.33 at R=1.5" in the window map), T0=19-26 K. Envelope N: s=0.14-0.27" (30-60 pc), ff(0.26")=0.32-0.52 (window mean 0.3-0.65), ff(0.18")=0.44-0.70. The N 12CO peak map is filamentary/clumpy around the HCN centre (peak-channel structure 0.7" south of it) so a single circular core is a poor description there: N size and ff are indicative only.
results.uncertainty: Profile-model envelope (above) dominates; statistical error within one model s +-0.04" (S), +-0.05" (N), ff(0.26") +-0.03 (S), +-0.08 (N). The extended 'pedestal' (4-7 K RJ) could be real extended emission or 12m missing flux (11% 12m deficit vs the 0.82" cube at >=0.57"); not separated. Sub-0.18" clumping cannot be excluded by any smooth fit. Peak-channel and window means agree. 13CO cannot be compared (Q32c).

results.value: Rigorous lower limits (ff=1, optically-thick-corrected with tau of Q30 for R(12/13)=40-90): from the NATIVE 0.18" peak T_b (34.8 K S, 15.6 K N RJ): Tk(S)>=40 K, Tk(N)>=21 K (at 0.26": S>=36, N>=18-19 K; the p0039 1" values S>=37, N>=19 K are thus slightly improved at S). Tk if the gas is SMOOTH inside the resolved core (T0 deconvolved, ff=1 within the core; pedestal excluded): S 34-53 K (Gauss+pedestal 39 K, 2D fits 38-39 K, free-size 34-35 K, Moffat 42 K, exponential 52 K); N 18-33 K (Gauss+pedestal 19 K, free-size 20 K, Moffat 21 K, exponential 28 K, 2D fits 28-32 K); window-mean version S 26-39 K, N 13-18 K. results.quantity: Q22a: joint N+S model comparison: one SHARED extended zone + separate cores (chi2 14.1, k=17, lnZ -52.5, BIC 73) beats independent envelopes (k=22, lnZ -60.9, dlnZ +8.5, BIC 91) and beats 'each nucleus a single state' (lnZ -77.3, dlnZ +24.9, chi2 62.6 mostly N 52) and cores only (chi2 133); the N single-state rejection survives envelope sharing and cross-nucleus leakage but rests on the combination of HCN and HCO+ 10 arcsec lines
results.value: Base run (Tbg 2.73 K, 4 seeds; chi2 = profile minimum over final particles; k free params; lnZ mean [seed sd]): cores only k=12 chi2 132.7 lnZ -118.3[0.9] BIC 174; same-state per nucleus k=14 62.6 (N 52.3, S 10.2) -77.3[0.7] BIC 111; shared envelope sh k=17 14.1 (N 8.3, S 5.7) -52.5[0.7] BIC 73.0; sh with separate fillings k=18 15.7 -54.4[1.1] BIC 78; independent envelopes sep k=22 15.1 (N 10.7, S 4.4) -60.9[1.1] BIC 91.4; hypothesis shH (Tc 10-25, Te 50-150 K) k=17 14.0 -49.9[0.8] BIC 73.0. => shared envelope vs independent: dlnZ +8.5, dBIC -18 (same data fitted with 5 fewer parameters at equal chi2: the independent envelopes double-count the same gas). Single-state-per-nucleus (the Q20 picture extended to 10 arcsec) vs shared envelope: dlnZ +24.9 in the base run. Sensitivity of this dlnZ(sh - same): Tbg 5 K +26.0; 10 arcsec scale sigma 30%: +26.1; other-core weight 0 / 1: +26.8 / +17.9; drop 10 arcsec 4-3: +24.1; drop 2-1: +24.0; drop all HCN 10 arcsec: +5.5 (chi2 same 20.9 vs 11.2); drop all HCO+ 10 arcsec: +4.8; leave one line out (HCN 2-1,3-2,4-3, HCO+ 2-1,3-2,4-3): +25.0/+17.7/+21.9/+25.0/+19.5/+21.3. So no single line or flux scale produces the second state; but once one whole species is removed the preference falls to dlnZ ~5 (about 3 sigma-equivalent), i.e. it is carried by the HCN-vs-HCO+ pattern of the 10 arcsec lines vs the 1.7 arcsec ladders together. Independent-envelope variants (sep) fit equally well with free 10 arcsec scales (sg30: chi2 9.6) and the shared model remains preferred in every variant (dlnZ vs sep 3-10). The N rather than S origin: same-state chi2(N)=52 vs chi2(S)=10; round-1 per-nucleus result (dlnZ +23 at N, +2.9 for S) is therefore reproduced with the other nucleus' core leaked in.
results.uncertainty: lnZ seed sd 0.4-1.1 (4 seeds); profile chi2 from best of final particles (+-1)

results.quantity: Q22c: N versus S and consistency with p0041: the HCN/HCO+ N-S contrast is carried by the N core (single-state N rejected) but the temperatures of cores and shared envelope do not differ significantly between N and S; N core posterior is low-T/high-n with a Tbg-dependent hot branch, in line with the bimodal Tk of p0041
results.value: Same-state per nucleus: chi2(N)=52, chi2(S)=10 -> a second (extended, lower-density, tau~1) zone is needed for N; S is fitted by a single state in the 1.7 arcsec+10 arcsec data when its own envelope is allowed (round 1) but with the shared envelope both nuclei need the common extended zone (sh is preferred over 'same' by dlnZ +25 jointly, the N part carrying most of it). Tc_N 16 [12,32] vs Tc_S 20.5 [13.5,32] K: P(Tc_N>=Tc_S)=0.41 (log prior), 0.57 (linear prior), 0.73 at Tbg 5 K, i.e. no N-S difference; Tc_N at Tbg 5 K is 30 [19,66] K, wide and sensitive to the background temperature, as is the p0041 N posterior (bimodal: Tk at its 300 K cap vs cold/dense branch; N(HCN)/N(HCO+) excess only ~2 sigma). In the present fit N has N_HCO+/N_HCN(core)=0.1 vs S ~7 at core level (HCN-rich N core; HCO+-rich S core), which is the same direction as p0041's HCN/HCO+ excess at N, but the column-ratio is poorly constrained (N(HCN)c 10^16.4 [10^16.2,10^17.0] vs N(HCO+)c 10^15.4 [10^15.2,10^16.0] at N; N 10^15.8 vs 10^16.6 at S) and should be read with p0041's ~2 sigma caveat; no claim of chemical difference is made. The CO floor test of round 1 (Q22d) is unchanged. Temperature labels: because Te is an independent parameter and the cores' T posteriors are listed per nucleus, no 'core/envelope' label swapping occurs in the joint fit; the swap seen in round 1 at Tbg 5 K in independent M2 fits is a feature of the unshared model.
results.uncertainty: see Q22b

results.quantity: Q22e: mass fractions and abundance constraints from the shared-envelope fit: core mass fraction of the HCN-traced gas within 10 arcsec = 0.009 [0.003,0.05] (S) and 0.08 [0.02,0.39] (N), independent of X(HCN) but proportional to the assumed envelope area; M_core(S) <= Mdyn(0.58e8) needs X(HCN) >~ 4e-9; the cores are clumpy (path 0.1-1 pc at X=1e-8, filling <0.02 of 66 pc)
results.value: Conventions: mu=2.8 m_H, D=40 Mpc (194 pc/arcsec), X(HCN)=N_HCN/N_H2 equal in cores and envelope, core area pi*(FWHM/2)^2 with pedestal-inclusive HCN 3-2 FWHM 0.455 (S)/0.507 (N) arcsec x core filling; envelope = filling x pi*(5 arcsec)^2 (one 10 arcsec circle; the N and S apertures overlap, the shared envelope is counted once per aperture). Shared envelope (median): X=1e-9/3e-9/1e-8/3e-8: M_core(S)=2.3e8/7.8e7/2.3e7/7.8e6 Msun, M_core(N)=1.9e9/6.3e8/1.9e8/6.3e7, M_env(10 arcsec)=1.8e10/6.1e9/1.8e9/6.1e8; core fraction S 0.009 [0.003,0.053], N 0.084 [0.017,0.39] (independent-envelope fit: S 0.023 [0.006,0.10], N 0.076 [0.018,0.52]). Core path length N_H2/n: S 1.0/0.33/0.10/0.03 pc, N 9.8/3.3/1.0/0.33 pc for X=1e-9..3e-8 (independent: S 11/3.6/1.1/0.36, N 23/7.7/2.3/0.77): all << the 50-66 pc core size, so the nuclei are not uniform space-filling HCN clouds but ensembles of dense clumps (filling factor along the line of sight L/66 pc ~ 0.002-0.15 at X=1e-8..1e-9, over and above eta_core); this is a constraint on clumping rather than on temperature. Fraction of the posterior with L_core<=66 pc and L_env<=500 pc: S 0.84/0.94/0.99/1.0, N 0.90/0.98/1.0/1.0 (shared; X as above). Self-consistency with Mdyn(S, 48 pc)=0.58e8 (Q5f): P(M_core<=Mdyn) = 0.09/0.39/0.74/0.91 for X=1e-9/3e-9/1e-8/3e-8 (shared; 0.02/0.15/0.52/0.84 independent), so X(HCN)>~4e-9 (shared; >~1e-8 independent) is needed for the core not to exceed the dynamical mass; the round-1 M_core(S)=1.5e8 at X=1e-8 was a consequence of the independent-envelope fit and a larger eta*N core. M_env(10 arcsec) at X=1e-9 (1.8e10) is of order or above the total molecular gas of the system and X<~2e-9 is disfavoured on that ground (CO-based total mass not re-derived here, no CO-derived mass in the team forum). The mass fractions scale with the adopted envelope area (10 arcsec circle); with a larger area the core fraction falls proportionally. H13CN(4-3) test: unchanged from round 1 (S consistent with HCN/H13CN>4 for R>=30 in 54-90%; N needs 12C/13C>~50-100).
results.uncertainty: median [16,84] given in the value text; 4 seeds pooled

results.quantity: Q22f: verdict (round 2): a joint two-component model (cool 12-32 K cores + one shared extended zone, Te=53 [34,78] K) fits the 1.7 and 10 arcsec ladders (chi2 14 for 32 data, k=17) far better than the single-phase core of Q20 (chi2 133) and than a single state per nucleus (dlnZ +25, driven by N), but the data do not require the envelope to be hot (P(Te>=50)=0.2-0.6, prior-dependent; Tc_S=20 [14,32] K as in Q20)
results.value: Summary: (1) cores only cannot fit 10 arcsec (chi2 133, chi2 of the 10 arcsec lines alone 24-28 per nucleus). (2) The shared envelope removes the double counting of independent envelopes (dlnZ +8.5 over independent, 5 fewer parameters, same chi2). (3) The single-state alternative is rejected by dlnZ +18..+26 in every sensitivity variant except when a whole species is dropped (+5): 10 arcsec flux-scale sigma 30%, other-core weight 0/1, Tbg 5 K, dropping 4-3 or 2-1, leave-one-line-out; a separate second T is not required, a second (lower-density, lower-column, filling ~0.26) zone is. (4) The temperature of that zone is poorly constrained: 53 [34,78] K at Tbg 2.73 K, 35 [25,51] K at Tbg 5 K; P(Te>=50) 0.55/0.18 (prior 0.41), 0.63/0.21 (linear-T prior; prior 0.71); the hypothesis of the item (Tc 10-25 K, Te>=50 K) fits as well as the free model (chi2 14.0 vs 14.1) and is not excluded, but is not demanded. (5) Cores: Tc 16 [12,32] (N), 20.5 [13.5,32] (S) K, the Q20 17-25 K S core is recovered; N-S difference not significant. (6) Cores hold 1-10% of the HCN-traced mass within 10 arcsec and have path lengths <<66 pc at X>=1e-9: clumpy cores. Still open: uv-matched (tapered) re-imaging of 10 arcsec ladders for N, S and midpoint (current 10 arcsec numbers are team-b p0028 values, one flux scale per band), IR-pumping Tbg, X(HCN) from H13CN with deeper data, dense-gas fraction from independent CO mass.
results.uncertainty: see Q22a-e

assumptions.value: Restored raw visibilities (continuum NOT subtracted by the archive; here: continuum from line-free channels per baseline/row, |v-2780|<=350 km/s integrated): Xb55 2 EBs (HCN/HCO+ 2-1), Xb4f 3 EBs (3-2), Xb4d 1 EB (3-2, team-b restore). assumptions.name: method

results.value: Observed binned Re(V) R32/R21 = 0.80, 0.99, 0.84, 0.77 (6-8/8-10/10-14/14-20 kl). Injection with NO fall in the extended ratio (R_ext 0.54 for both J) but the measured core ratios gives binned R32/R21 = 0.91+-0.03, 0.91+-0.04, 0.89+-0.03, 0.86+-0.04: the compact-component leakage alone biases the binned ratio LOW by ~10%; injected 15% fall gives 0.84, 0.86, 0.85, 0.83. Observed binned values (mean 0.85) therefore lie between the two scenarios (1 sigma from each; cannot be separated), i.e. the binned 15% 'fall' is explained by cores. Core-removed fit recovers R_ext32/R_ext21 = 1.01+-0.08 (no fall) and 0.89+-0.08 (fall) in injection (bias <0.02, 0.89 vs 0.85 truth), so the method is unbiased but its injected scatter 0.08 cannot separate 1.0 from 0.85 at 2 sigma. Observed R_ext(3-2 Xb4f)/R_ext(2-1 Xb55) = 1.05 (10" Gaussian, u>8 kl), 1.01 (u>10), 0.87/0.77 (6"), 1.26/1.38 (15"); Xb4d (u>10 kl only, chi2_r 4-10) gives 0.6-0.7. Real-data uncertainty (baseline bootstrap) +-0.18 (10", u>8), 0.26 (u>10), larger for 15"; EB jackknife range of R_ext32 0.42-0.59. Adopted: R_ext(3-2)/R_ext(2-1) = 1.0 (+0.3,-0.4) incl. profile and Xb4f/Xb4d systematics, i.e. consistent with both no change and a 15-25% fall. RADEX (HCN/HCO+ with X tuned to R21=0.54, Tk 20-150 K, n 1e4-1e6, N(HCO+) 3e14-3e16): expected R32/R21 = 0.5-0.93, typically 0.7-0.85 (0.65-0.76 at 20-50 K and n<=1e5; ->0.85-0.93 at 150 K, n>=1e5, high N) -- a modest fall is the physically expected outcome, so the measurement (limit R32/R21 > ~0.65 at 2 sigma) does not discriminate between sub-thermal and thermalised extended gas.

results.quantity: Q36b: radiation field (background mean intensity) at the HCN/HCO+ transitions implied by the continuum, and the equivalent blackbody Tbg
results.target: S core, N core, extended (10") envelope
results.value: Compact cores: J_bg = J_CMB + eta*Tb_cont(nu). Nominal (eta=0.7, 50% dust, intrinsic Tb 0.80 K S / 0.18 K N at 258 GHz, dust Tb~nu^1.8, ff Tb~nu^-2.1): equivalent blackbody Tbg at HCN 1-0/2-1/3-2/4-3 = S 5.7/4.0/4.3/5.2 K, N 3.4/3.1/3.2/3.7 K (the 1-0 value is driven by the extrapolated free-free and is uncertain). Dust-only bracket (all continuum treated as dust, eta=1): S 2.9/3.5/4.8/6.7 K, N 2.8/2.9/3.4/4.4 K. High (x2 sub-beam clumping, eta=1): S 3.0/4.1/6.1/8.8 K, N 2.8/3.1/3.9/5.2 K. So the S core sees an effective Tbg of ~4-6 K at 3-2/4-3 (J_bg 0.7-1.8 K vs 0.12/0.03 K for the CMB), the N core ~3-4 K. Envelope: the observed 10" beam-mean continuum Tb is 5-8 mK (<=10% of the CMB J at 258 GHz); even assuming 10x sub-beam concentration (Tb_local 0.07 K at 258 GHz) the envelope sees Tbg_eq = 2.7/2.8/3.0/3.6 K (1-0..4-3). A uniform Tbg=5 K, as in the earlier Q22 sensitivity test, therefore over-states the field for the envelope by an order of magnitude in J(266 GHz) (1.08 K vs 0.12-0.19 K).
results.uncertainty: eta 0.5-1, dust fraction 0.5-1, clumping x1-2 -> J_bg(S core, 266 GHz) 0.5-1.8 K; envelope J_bg(266 GHz) 0.12-0.19 K

results.quantity: Q36c: Q22 shared-envelope fit rerun with the continuum-based radiation field: does it favour a hot (>=50 K) or warm (~35-45 K) envelope?
results.target: joint N+S, 1.7" and 10" HCN/HCO+ ladders, shared envelope (env='sh') and separate envelopes ('sep')
results.value: Radiation field from Q36b applied to the cores (per nucleus, frequency dependent) with the envelope at the CMB (+0.02-0.07 K local dust): P(Te>=50 K) = 0.42 (nominal), 0.35 (dust-only), 0.56 (high), 0.43 (envelope with extra local dust, nominal cores), 0.49/0.37 (envhi with nominal/high cores) vs 0.43 for CMB-only (6 seeds x 12000 particles each; seed-to-seed scatter of P is 0.1-0.4). Envelope Te median 45-52 K (16-84%: 31-81 K), cores Tc_N 18-31 K, Tc_S 18-25 K, i.e. the conclusion of Q22 (cool 17-25 K cores, envelope hot-or-warm, not required hot) is unchanged and robust to the physically implied radiation field. In contrast the uniform Tbg=5 K applied to everything lowers P(Te>=50) to 0.13 (Te 33 [24,47] K); the same drop (0.11, Te 31 K) occurs if only the ENVELOPE gets Tbg=5 K with CMB cores, so the earlier P(Te>=50) 0.55->0.18 flip is entirely an envelope-background effect, and the observed 10" continuum (Tb 5-8 mK) excludes a 5 K background for the envelope. Evidence differences are small: ln Z (mean of 6) -53.1 (CMB), -51.9 (nominal), -53.0 (dust-only), -51.5 (high), -54.8 (uniform 5 K), -54.9 (envelope-only 5 K): the radiation-field models are mildly preferred (dlnZ ~+1 to +1.6 +-1.5) and uniform 5 K mildly disfavoured (dlnZ ~-1.7). Separate-envelope fits: P(Te>=50) N/S = 0.30/0.42 (nominal), 0.38/0.30 (CMB), 0.06/0.08 (uniform 5 K). Answer: the continuum favours Tbg(eff) ~ 3-4 K in the N core, ~4-6 K (at J>=2) in the S core and ~2.7-3 K in the envelope, so Q22's envelope is 'warm-to-hot' (Te~47 K, P(>=50 K) ~0.4+-0.2), not decisively either; the hot/warm question cannot be settled by the radiation field.
results.uncertainty: P(Te>=50)=0.43 +-0.20 (seed scatter, 6 runs) for realistic fields; Te 47 K (+18,-14)

results.quantity: Q38: Is the 5-8 mK 10" continuum Tb a lower limit (12m-only missing extended dust) and what does a FIR-SED global dust disk bound for the envelope background?
results.target: NGC 3256 N/S 10" envelope; Xb55/Xb4f/Xb47 12m continuum (170.7/257.7/346.5 GHz)
results.value: YES, in principle a lower limit: the 12m MRS is only ~11" (Band 6; scaled from Cycle-5 C43-1/-3 handbook MRS 28.5"/16.2" at 100 GHz -> 11.1"/6.3" at 258 GHz; ~16.7-9.5" B5, 8.2-4.7" B7; inferred from beam sizes, not from visibilities), so any dust disk with FWHM >~10-15" is entirely resolved out. Global dust from the Michiyama+2020 FIR fluxes (S160=93.5 Jy; Td 25-34 K, beta 1.5-2, optically thin extrapolation, tau_258<~3e-3) is 140-690 mJy at 258 GHz (255 mJy for Td=30, beta=1.8) vs ~35-70 mJy (N+S, in a 10.5" beam, ~50% dust) recovered. If that global dust sits in a Gaussian disk of FWHM F, its intrinsic central Tb_RJ(258 GHz) = 47/21/12/5 mK for F=10/15/20/30" (Td 30, beta 1.8; up to 85 mK for beta 1.5, 127 mK for Td 25 K, F=10"), i.e. <=10-35% of J_CMB(258)=134 mK for F>=15" (up to 0.6-1x for the extreme F=10", Td=25 K cases). Envelope background J_bg = J_CMB + eta*Tb_dust(nu): equivalent Tbg for HCN/HCO+ 2-1/3-2/4-3 = 2.73-2.77/2.74-2.90/2.75-3.24 K for F>=15", Td>=30 K, eta 0.5-1, and at most 2.89/3.23/3.89 K for the extreme F=10", Td=25 K, beta=1.5, eta=1 case. This is within the q36 'envhi' scenario already run (Tb258=70 mK: Tbg_eq 2.74/2.80/3.03/3.62 K), for which Q22 P(Te>=50 K)=0.49 (nominal cores) / 0.37 (high cores), Te median 50/44 K vs 0.43 CMB-only: no change. A background >=5 K (the case that flipped Q22 to 0.13) would need the whole FIR dust in a <~5" disk, which is excluded because the nuclear cores are resolved at 0.24-1" with 10" Tb<=0.6 K at 0.24" and the beam-integrated 10" flux is only ~35 mJy per nucleus. The 5-8 mK 10" Tb is thus a lower limit, but the missing extended dust raises J_bg(env) at most to Tbg_eq<=3.2 K at 3-2 and <=3.9 K at 4-3 (<=3.1 K / 3.4 K for the plausible F>=15", Td~30 K); the Q36 conclusion (Tbg 2.73 K adequate for the envelope, hot envelope not required nor excluded) stands.
results.uncertainty: MRS from configuration inference (+-30%); disk FWHM unknown (10-30" bracketed); FIR extrapolation of 160 um to mm with beta 1.5-2 and Td 25-34 K (factor ~4 in S258); part of the global flux is the nuclei themselves (so diffuse dust is overestimated by up to ~30%); 'eta' geometry 0.5-1; ff not included (negligible at >=177 GHz, affects 1-0 only).

interpretation:
Line inventory (corrected): besides HCN and HCO+ (J=2-1,3-2,4-3) and CS 7-6, CH3OH is detected (Band 5 165 GHz Q-branch J=1-3 at 27 sigma; 2(0)-1(-1) E at 254.015 GHz at 10 sigma), SO 5(4)-4(3) (Band 5, 8 sigma) is detected, HOC+ is tentative; everything else is a limit, blended or an edge artefact. CH3OH is cold/subthermal (Q-branch J>=4 and Eu>45 K lines absent; LTE Trot~9 K, but LTE and RADEX fits are poor) and extended: the Xb4d (0.9") CH3OH flux is only ~55% of the 9"-beam value, and in Xb4d it peaks on the Bridge and a W clump, not on the N and S nuclei (CH3OH/HCO+ 0.05 there vs <0.015 at the nuclei) - a shock/low-excitation tracer signature that agrees qualitatively with Harada+2018. The extended disk is defined (Xb55 HCO+ 2-1 S/N>5 at r>8", HCN/HCO+(2-1)=0.51) but is not detected in the 3-2/4-3 data with the available sensitivity/zero-level. The southern blue-shifted component 1.9" south of S is statistically solid (7-12 sigma after null calibration, 0 null peaks above 8 sigma in 583 beams), has no red counterpart, is not a PSF-sidelobe copy of S, and has HCN/HCO+(3-2)~1.8 versus 0.4 at S; it is a separate broad component at ~2560-2650 km/s. The N and S nuclei are separable in Xb4b, Xb4d, Xb4f, Xb47 (not in Band 5). The opacity test (H13CN) can only give HCN/H13CN>7-9 (conditional on the CO-wing model). Raw HCN/HCO+ (3-2) peak ratios (N 0.6-1.0, S 0.4-0.5) are preliminary and not beam matched across OUS (Q1). Q1 (rev. 2): At matched 1.05" the northern nucleus has HCN/HCO+ 3-2 = 0.83+-0.04 and the southern (AGN) nucleus 0.40+-0.02 (N/S = 2.0-2.1, constant over the line core, insensitive to the velocity window to <=2.5% and to Xb4b vs Xb4d); the AGN has the lowest ratio, i.e. no HCN enhancement at the AGN (as Harada+2018). Blended 6.5"/10" aperture ratios hide this (N/S 1.1-1.2), but deblending the native-beam Band 7 4-3 map with the 1" templates recovers N/S = 1.9+-0.5 (N 0.47, S 0.25) and CS 7-6/HCO+ 3-2 is the same at N and S within errors (S/N 1.09+-0.48; HCN/CS 1.9x lower at S, 1.2 sigma: weak); at 2-1 (9" beam) the N-S pair is not separable (contrast 1-3, template-limited). The ladders (3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2: HCN 0.35/0.39 (N), HCO+ 0.43/0.48) are strongly sub-thermal and the same at N and S within 14% (HCN 4-3/3-2 lower at S, 1.8 sigma): a quick RADEX grid gives n(H2) <~ 1e5 cm-3 and Tkin >~ 30 K at N, and requires N(HCN)/N(HCO+) >= 3 at both nuclei; since the ladders do not differ, the factor-2 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast must come mainly from the HCN/HCO+ abundance (or HCN column/opacity) rather than density or temperature (equal-X disfavoured at ~2 sigma only). The disk 2-1 HCN/HCO+ is 0.47-0.50, 15-25% below the nuclei at the same beam; its 3-2 deficit is fully consistent with missing short spacings in Xb4f for a 13-14" scale structure (B_min = 8.7 m assumed), so no excitation difference of the disk can be claimed from HCO+; the HCN 3-2 deficit is larger than recovery alone explains but depends on the zero level. The Soutflow blue-wing HCN/HCO+ is 1.2-1.8 depending on estimator (candidate, single position, HCO+ wing 5-7 sigma). Resolution forces an 'active region versus disk' comparison at J=2-1 and for the disk, but not at J=3-2 and 4-3, where N and S are distinguishable. Q3 (outflow, revised): dense gas (HCN 12.6 sigma, HCO+ 5 sigma) is detected 1.9" (370 pc) S of the S nucleus at the blue lobe of the southern edge-on outflow (MEDIUM confidence; a disk warp/tidal feature is not rejected). In fixed a-priori apertures with velocity relative to the local centroid the blue-half HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ratio is 1.0-1.4, robustly above S (0.15-0.46) but not significantly different from N (1.13) and Bridge (1.3); the earlier 1.7 was peak-selected (+10% noise bias, rest spatial gradient); the whole broad component has 0.72-0.8 (N-like). Blends (CH3NH2, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH, CH3OH) are limited to <=10-18% of the HCN blue side by LTE fits to other lines; HDO untestable. No dense-gas wing at N: 3 sigma <2-4% (HCN, blue 225-750 km/s) of core, mass <=1.3e6-1.4e7 Msun; weak 2-3 sigma hints at North-OF-Blue are not significant. Soutflow dense mass 1.4-6.5e6 Msun (alpha 3-10), ~6-37% of the S-outflow CO high-velocity mass depending on X20. Q4 (final): the J=1-0 literature data (Harada+2018 Table 13, 1.7 arcsec: HCN/HCO+ N 0.96, S 0.645) show that ~60% (in log) of the N/S contrast of the 3-2 ratio (1.9-2.0) is already present at 1-0 (1.49): the contrast is mostly J-independent, not excitation. Joint RADEX fits (including 1-0, a separate-density class, BIC/marginal likelihood) prefer both lines thick with HCN more subthermal than HCO+ (Tex ~7 vs ~11 K; HCN tau32 >~2, >~10 for common n; A and separate-n F2 indistinguishable) and reject thin-HCN/abundance-only classes (Delta chi2>=65), also without the Band-5 2-1 ratios; different filling at equal Tex (B) fails the independent 1-0 prediction. Between N and S the data require the HCN (or HCO+) column ratio to change by 1.8-3x, not n or Tkin; N is poorly fitted by every one-zone model, and 8 data cannot constrain two-component models. CS and low-J ratios weakly favour an HCN deficit over an HCO+ enhancement (HCN/CS and HNC/HCO+ lower at S, HCO+/CS equal) but this is <=1.2 sigma in the data. H13CN (HCN/H13CN >8.3 N, >4 S) cannot test opacity: the models predict 17-68. HCN v2=1f limits (alpha<0.03-0.09, Tvib<290-430 K) do not exclude CON-like pumping (200-300 K). H13CN (HCN/H13CN >8.3 N, >4 S) cannot test opacity: the models predict 17-68. HCN v2=1f limits (alpha<0.03-0.09, Tvib<290-430 K) do not exclude CON-like pumping (200-300 K). SO limits refer to the central 9x6" beam and to equally extended emission; CH3OH is extended and off-nuclear (<0.013/<0.017 at the nuclei, 0.052 at the Bridge). With X(HCN)=1e-8 the fitted HCN column implies Sigma 2e4-1e5 Msun/pc2, 4-20x above the CO maximum: a tension, not an explanation. The 100-pc-scale source is resolved at 0.25" (dilution 0.8-0.9).

Q9 (velocity-resolved ratios, revised after review): HCN/HCO+ 3-2 is NOT strictly flat in velocity, and the supported statements are: (i) at the N nucleus at 0.30" (r<0.25", 50 pc) the window-integrated ratio is 0.92-1.04 across +-100 km/s (~12% blue-to-red decline) and 1.05+-0.13 in the 100-260 km/s wings (no significant rise; core 0.98+-0.013); (ii) at 1.05" (r<0.5") there is a significant monotonic trend, +0.08+-0.006 per 100 km/s, with the wings (100-260 km/s stacked 1.19+-0.10, lower limit >1.2 at 150-250 km/s) 4 sigma above the core (0.77); the same trend appears when Xb4b is convolved to 1.05" (+0.072+-0.008) and vanishes at 0.30" (-0.003+-0.013), HCN centroids lie 0.04-0.13" closer to the nucleus than HCO+, and an injection of the measured radial ratio gradient with identical kinematics reproduces ~60-70% of the slope (+0.049): it is predominantly a beam/spatial-mixing effect with a residual (+0.02-0.03 per 100 km/s) not reproduced by the injection, which could be an HCN wing excess of a few 0.1 in the ratio from gas with a different ratio or lower HCO+ opacity; (iii) the S deficit is present at all velocities with HCN detected: 0.37-0.45 from the core to |v|~260 km/s (stacked wings 0.44+-0.03 at 1.05", 0.44+-0.05 at 0.30"), i.e. 2-3x below N, valid for |v|<~260 km/s where HCN is detected (HCO+-only beyond); (iv) the Bridge wing ratio rises to >=1 (1.35+-0.32 stacked 100-260 km/s vs core 0.44). Physically (RADEX with equal filling): the N core ratio ~1 with per-channel Tb(HCN)/Tb(HCO+)=0.96-0.97 over the full profile is what two optically thick (tau>~3), thermalised lines of the same Tex and width produce (ratio -> 1 for X<=3), with peak Tb of only 1.5-2.8 K implying filling factors 0.02-0.35; it does not constrain the abundance ratio X for X<=3. S (0.42) cannot be two thick equal-Tex lines: it needs lower N(HCN)/N(HCO+)<=1 with moderate HCN opacity, or Tex(HCN)<Tex(HCO+) at lower density; the fact that the S ratio is constant over the whole profile argues for a ratio set by the gas as a whole rather than by the line core saturating. An opacity-driven core dip is not seen anywhere. The 4-3/3-2 ladder (6.5") separates N and S only through Xb4d weights: R(4-3/3-2, Tb) is 0.46 (N) vs 0.30 (S) for HCN and 0.575 vs 0.40 for HCO+, and the red-wing HCO+ drop (0.50 -> 0.40) is mostly (~2/3) N/S weighting, since red HCO+ flux is 81% S.

Q2 (non-LTE ranges; credible intervals, not best fits; revised after the temperature-floor and Tbg tests): both nuclei are described by optically thick (tau32 HCN ~5-50), sub-thermal HCN and HCO+ (Tex 6-11 K, Tkin>>Tex) in gas of log n(H2)~4.5-5.5 (3e4-3e5 cm-3) with column degeneracies of ~0.5 dex. Density is not distinguishable between N and S. With no temperature floor S is Tkin ~15-50 K (T>=80 K excluded at >3 sigma) and N is 25-100 K (class dependent; a warmer N is only suggestive). The robust N/S difference is the excitation pattern: Tex(HCN)/Tex(HCO+)~0.86 at N vs 0.63 at S (the only both-thick solution that reproduces R32=0.39 and the 1-0 ratio), valid for a background Tbg<=5 K (continuum-based Tbg,eff 3.0-3.7 K); for Tbg>=10 K the equal-Tex solution is preferred at S. Bridge, disk, wing and outflow regions have only one or two ratios: R32 alone gives n>=1e5 cm-3 and no temperature constraint, and the single-molecule ladders are band-degenerate (T 10-150 K, 2.5-5 dex in n). Abundances: X(HCN) is not measured; the CO surface density demands X(HCN)>~1e-7 (Sigma_max 470 Msun/pc2) or >~1e-8 (Sigma 1e4) if the HCN column fills the beam. The H13CN limits and the velocity-resolved ratios do not add constraints; CS is class dependent. Q12 update (round 2, supersedes the earlier Q12 paragraph and the 'chi2 19-23/8' statistic): the fit statistic is the profile chi2 of 7 independent data (R32 removed; it equals R10*(H32/10)/(O32/10)), with Gaussian nuisance penalties, calibrated by simulation, plus the marginal likelihood for model comparison. A compact optically thick core plus envelope does not 'fix' the N one-zone fit in any testable sense: two-component models have as many effective parameters as data (8 vs 7) and chi2~0, and the one-zone N misfit (chi2 9.1/3, p=0.03 at fixed geometry) disappears (chi2 3.2/3, p=0.36) when the extended filling at 1.7" and the compact size take the widths measured from the 0.25/0.95/1.7/5.7" growth curve (N compact FWHM 0.44" [0.25-0.57], u=1.6 [1.1-3.0]). The evidence for two components at N (dlnZ=+3.0 at fixed geometry) is not significant (14.5% of data-consistent one-zone truths with wrong sizes exceed +3; 0% with right geometry) and turns to -1.7 with measured geometry, where the statistic has no power to tell one-zone from two-component truths. The H13CN limit removes 50-80% of the N two-comp posterior mass (compact tau32 median 23-37 -> 5-14); the claims n_c>1e6 and tau32 10-100 are prior-edge and geometry dependent. S needs no second component; Tkin 19-23 K (14-35 K), P(>=80 K)<=0.06 holds against geometry, floor, Tbg 5 K and H13CN. N compact Tkin is unconstrained (12-96 K); the N-vs-S contrast is not significant (joint over 16 deblend variants: P(T_N>T_S) 0.47-0.60 with measured geometry, 0.72-0.93 at fixed geometry). Confidence: N temperature low, S temperature medium-low, N-vs-S contrast low (unconstrained). A 1-0 map at matched ~1" resolution (only Harada+2018 1.7" 12m-only values are available) is the datum that would break the geometry degeneracy.

Q8: The N-vs-S excitation contrast of the dense gas (T43/T32 N/S 1.26-1.33 for HCN, 1.1 for HCO+; team-b p0015) is not established as a Tkin effect, and it is not a size effect either. (1) Size/filling alone with equal excitation gives <=1.1. (2) Xb4d/Xb4b 3-2 are lossy references (12-40% less 3-2 than Xb4f, S more than N) and cannot be used to say the contrast is 1; Xb4f is the uv-matched reference for Xb47 (same configuration class). (3) A uv forward model calibrated on all three Band-6 arrays (line and continuum) fits the array ratios well but cannot fix the absolute short-spacing loss of Xb4f/Xb47: if Xb4f/Xb47 were lossless the corrected HCN contrast is 1.18 [1.04,1.32]; with the physical minimum baseline (>=15 m) Xb47 loses 25-50% of the extended flux relative to Xb4f, S more than N, and the contrast is 0.96 [0.84,1.10]; the continuum Xb47/Xb4f N/S 1.20 (equal spectral index) points to the latter (HCN 1.03, HCO+ 0.92). Pooled: HCN 1.07 [0.89,1.26] (95% 0.76-1.42), HCO+ 1.00 [0.88,1.12]. (4) A ~10% HCN-specific excess over HCO+ (double ratio 1.11 [1.02,1.23]) survives the common-mode cancellation but is within the scatter of control position pairs (23-28% exceed it). (5) 70-97% of the 3-2/4-3 peak at these beams is extended gas (compact beam filling ~1%): the measured ratio refers to the extended gas, T_N/T_S ~0.8-1.9 (consistent with 1), and the nuclear dense gas at 0.4" is not constrained by the 4-6" ladder. Confidence low: the temperature difference between the nuclei is neither detected nor excluded at <=1.4 (95%). A ~1" 1-0/2-1 map from the same configuration as the 4-3 would break the degeneracy; it is not in the archive.

Q14: Chemistry (third axis of the research question). The data show no shock-chemistry signature that separates the nuclei from each other in CS, SO, SiS, HCN v2=1; SiO is untestable (limits 5-360x above Harada's ratio). The one varying species is CH3OH: extended (still rising at R=6"), peaked on the Bridge/W clump, detected at S (4.6 sigma at 6.3x3.8") and weak at N (1.2-1.6 sigma); the S>N CH3OH/HCO+ contrast is moderate (2.8-3.0 sigma per array; <1.5 sigma at <=4.45") and is not an S-nuclear source. Per H2 the contrast is ~8 at equal Tex but falls to ~2 if N is warmer/dustier-hot than S, as Q2 suggests, so it is not an established abundance difference. The comparison with Harada+2018 (largest SiO and CH3OH variation, S/N CH3OH ~4) is consistent for CH3OH: the Harada 96.74 data are 12-m-only Band 3 with MRS ~28" and the matched whole-line estimator reproduces his S and N 96.74/HCO+ within ~1 sigma in LTE at his own Trot; the earlier apparent x3 tension was an estimator artefact. CH3OH is sub-thermally excited (Tex(254) 5-7 K for n~1e5.5-1e6.5): LTE column densities are lower limits by 1.7-4.9x. Earlier p0001 claims (Trot 9 K, Q-branch excess, Band-5 Bridge enhancement) remain withdrawn as baseline-limited.

Q13: The southern blue lobe is a dense-gas feature (HCO+ 4-5 sigma, HCN excess 4.4 sigma at 1.05" in Xb4d); Xb4b (1 sigma) is consistent with it because its 1.05" sensitivity is too low and part of the excess may be extended; blends other than HDO are <=10-18%, and HDO would need to be lobe-specific by >=7-17x. We therefore keep 'dense gas in the S outflow' (medium) and treat HCN/HCO+>1 in the blue wing as probable but unproven; the whole-component ratio is 0.74+-0.15, not much above the nuclei (0.4-0.8). [ROUND2] Q13 calibration: the S-lobe HCN excess over k*HCO+ is 4.4 sigma pointwise but 3.0-3.2 sigma after correcting for the position choice (marginal); the HDO blend as its sole origin is chemically disfavoured (needs HDO/H2>~1e-7) but not excluded. [Q15 round] The red-shifted dense-gas ridge ~3.3" N of S (coincident with Michiyama+2018 OF-Red) is real in HCN 3-2 (5.9 sigma pointwise, recovered in Xb4b and in the baseline-free tapered cube) and tentative in HCO+; its origin (S counter-lobe vs Bridge/N-related) is undecided: symmetric wing velocity and flux and the OF-Red coincidence favour a counter-lobe, while the N/Bridge-like core velocity and the continuous red tongue to N favour an inter-nuclear/N association. Bipolarity of the dense S outflow is permitted, not established. [Q5 round 2] At 0.24" the N nucleus is a ~50 pc (HCO+ 0.26-0.29" geometric FWHM) dense core on a 100x25 pc ridge with a flat rotation curve (Vlos 65+-3 km/s, i.e. ~130 km/s deprojected at i=30 deg; Mdyn(<97 pc) ~4e8 Msun, factor 0.7-1.6 from the inclination) and a centrally peaked intrinsic dispersion (63-79 km/s at R~0 to 24 km/s at 1"), of which beam smearing is 24-25 km/s of the observed 55-70; the S nucleus is a similar-size (0.25-0.34") HCO+ core in an E-W disk that is only roughly rotating (PA 110+-4 deg, Vlos 78+-5 km/s, chi2_red 14; Mdyn(<97 pc) ~1e8 within a factor 2; no usable gradient at R<0.4"). Virial and rotation masses agree, so the dense-gas widths are gravitational, not outflow broadening. HCN is not more extended than HCO+: at matched 0.30" resolution r50 is 0.50 vs 0.56" (N) and 0.37 vs 0.44" (S), the HCN/HCO+ ratio is ~1.0 within 0.3" at N and falls to 0.4 at 1-1.5" (agrees with team-b p0005 and team-a p0005-r02), and flat 0.37 at S; the round-1 HCN-larger-than-HCO+ result is withdrawn and a common filling factor is supported to ~15%. Line and 1.1 mm centroids coincide to <=0.1" (N) and <=0.05" (S) (<0.4 beam), thermal position errors <=0.01"; Gaussian sizes below ~0.1" and all sub-clump fits other than N-core HCO+, S-core HCO+ and the S-E HCN clump are unconstrained.
caveats: Peak-pixel intensities use different native beams per OUS; no cross-OUS ratio in this item is beam matched (Q1/Q6).

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.

Q1: ratio uncertainties are dominated by systematics (window truncation ~5%, absolute flux scale 10% per band); statistical errors are <=1% at the nuclei. Noise uses few line-free windows contaminated at times by weak lines (quietest quartile used), so faint-region limits are approximate.
Q1: regions use fixed nominal positions; the N ratio varies across its sub-clumps (IQR 0.05-0.09 at 1.05"), so a different aperture centre changes N by ~0.03-0.05.

Q1: the decline of HCN/HCO+ and the low 3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2 ladder ratios at 10" mix Band 5, 6 and 7 data with different resolved-out fractions (Q6: Xb4f is the most complete Band 6 set); they should be treated as inputs to RADEX with 14% errors, not as evidence for a nuclear difference.

Q1: the Xb55 2-1 "disk" may include beam wings of the nuclei and NEclump; the ring zero level (-1.2 to -2.0 Jy/b km/s) is not present in line-free channels, so the sign of the correction is uncertain.

Q1b: the deblending assumes a uniform ratio inside each template component and that the 1" 3-2 template traces the same gas as the coarse line; chi2_r of the fits is 7-44 even with a 3% floor, so formal errors are meaningless and template systematics (a factor ~2 on N/S flux ratios at 2-1) dominate. Only the 4-3 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast (1.9+-0.5) survives the injection test.

Q1b: the disk recovery model assumes B_min and a single Gaussian disk; the array identity is inferred from beam sizes (no uv information in the products). The zero-level (ring) correction of the disk maps changes the 3-2 ratio by a factor of 4, so disk 3-2 statements are limits.

Q1b: RADEX constraints come from 5 ratios and 4 parameters (1 dof), assume equal beam filling for all lines and a single (n, T) per region for HCN and HCO+; they bound n(H2) and X, not the absolute columns. The H13CN limit is conditional on the CO-wing model of p0001.

Q3 (round 2): outflow classification rests on kinematics (one-sided broad blue gas, mirror/control positions) and literature geometry, not CO; disk-warp/tidal origin unrejected. Blend limits cover CH3NH2, CH3OH, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH only (HDO and exotic species untested) and assume HCO+-like profiles. Xb4b (independent array) gives lower ratios (blue half 0.9-1.0 vs 1.2-1.4) and recovers ~55% of the flux: ratio systematics 10-25%. Noise is statistical (flux scale 5-10% common to all positions). The two-Gaussian split is shape-dependent (chi2/dof 2.6). N limits are for compact gas at 225-750 km/s LOS only; HCO+ red window contaminated by HCN v2=1f; HCN red window truncated at +693 km/s by the band edge. Dense masses: alpha 3-10 and r31 0.3-1 are assumptions; CO mass comparison uses the whole S-outflow CO HV mass (both lobes) so fractions are good to a factor ~2 only. RADEX is illustrative (no dof).

Q4: HCN v2=1f limits assume equal beam filling and thin vib line; IR pumping in a source much smaller than 47 pc would be diluted in all beams. SO 4_5-3_4 flux changed from 1.25 Jy/beam km/s (peak pixel, no wing subtraction) to 0.63+-0.08 K km/s (=0.97 Jy/beam km/s at 9.4x6.3") after fitting the HCO+ wing; Band-5 SO is blended N+S+Bridge. CH3OH maser test depends on the unknown flux recovery of Xb4f relative to Band 5; the 6_5-5_4 SO temperature limit scales the same way. HOC+ and HC15N hints are 3-3.5 sigma only. To settle: HCO+/H13CO+ or HC18O+ (not in band), matched 1-0 lines, and short-spacing Band 6 data.
Q4b: H13CN sits on the CO 3-2 red wing (core out of band); wing-model mismatch biases alpha by -0.02 to -0.11, comparable to the signal; only limits are quoted. 12C/13C 30-90 assumed.
Q4b: SO Trot limits assume thin LTE, f (Xb4f recovery) prior 0.5-1 and a blended N+S+Bridge 9x6" beam; not nuclear.

Q4c: all RADEX fits are one-zone (uniform sphere, escape probability), common Tkin, flat log priors on a 0.25-dex grid with Tkin>=30 K (posteriors for A/F sit at the 30 K edge) and N<=n+12.5; HCN tau posteriors saturate at the grid cap, so only lower limits are given. 8 data vs 4-7 parameters: chi2/BIC/lnZ rank models; the N nucleus is fitted marginally by one-zone models (chi2 19-23 here is a marginalised statistic; profile chi2 9.2/4 dof in Q12), two-component models are in Q12.

Q4c: the 1-0 data are at 1.7" (Harada, 12m-only) and 2.1x1.7" (Michiyama), the 3-2 ladders at 0.95-6": beam-dependent ratios (N: R32 0.93/0.85/0.75 at 0.25/0.93/1.7") and the 4-23% difference between Harada's and our 3-2 integrals are systematic errors not fully propagated; cross-band 3-2/1-0 scale handled as a 10% nuisance.

Q4c: N/dv scaling makes tau and Tex independent of the assumed cloud width, but the per-cloud columns, the number of clouds (>=3) and the Sigma comparison depend on dv, X(HCN)=1e-8 (assumed) and on the neglected coupling between overlapping clouds.

Q4c: CS 7-6 enters only through the Q1 template deblend (spread 20-30%) and a RADEX model with the HCO+ Tkin and n; the HCN deficit vs HCO+ enhancement question is undecided in the models and tentative in the low-J ratios (CS(2-1)/HCO+(1-0) excitation not modelled).

Q4c: SO/CH3OH shock limits are for a central 9x6" beam or for compact HCO+-like emission; literature values are from paper tables (Harada, Michiyama) or abstracts (others); HCN-vib/SO/CH3OH benchmarks in other galaxies were not verified.

Q4c: all RADEX fits are one-zone (uniform sphere, escape probability), common Tkin, flat log priors on a 0.25-dex grid with Tkin>=30 K (posteriors for A/F sit at the 30 K edge) and N<=n+12.5; HCN tau posteriors saturate at the grid cap, so only lower limits are given. 8 data vs 4-7 parameters: chi2/BIC/lnZ rank models; the N nucleus is fitted marginally by one-zone models (chi2 19-23 here is a marginalised statistic; profile chi2 9.2/4 dof in Q12), two-component models are in Q12.

Q4c: the 1-0 data are at 1.7" (Harada, 12m-only) and 2.1x1.7" (Michiyama), the 3-2 ladders at 0.95-6": beam-dependent ratios (N: R32 0.93/0.85/0.75 at 0.25/0.93/1.7") and the 4-23% difference between Harada's and our 3-2 integrals are systematic errors not fully propagated; cross-band 3-2/1-0 scale handled as a 10% nuisance.

Q4c: N/dv scaling makes tau and Tex independent of the assumed cloud width, but the per-cloud columns, the number of clouds (>=3) and the Sigma comparison depend on dv, X(HCN)=1e-8 (assumed) and on the neglected coupling between overlapping clouds.

Q4c: CS 7-6 enters only through the Q1 template deblend (spread 20-30%) and a RADEX model with the HCO+ Tkin and n; the HCN deficit vs HCO+ enhancement question is undecided in the models and tentative in the low-J ratios (CS(2-1)/HCO+(1-0) excitation not modelled).

Q4c: SO/CH3OH shock limits are for a central 9x6" beam or for compact HCO+-like emission; literature values are from paper tables (Harada, Michiyama) or abstracts (others); HCN-vib/SO/CH3OH benchmarks in other galaxies were not verified.

Q7: Xb4b outer annuli (>1.5") lose extended flux vs Xb4d (N 2-3": 0.30 vs 0.40); use Xb4d. Injection with real null noise gives a +0.09 bias at N 1.5-2" (~2.5 sigma): outer-annulus error floor +-0.05. The N-peak ratio ~1 is a flux ratio, not an abundance ratio.

Q9 (revised): errors are statistical nulls plus baseline-fit variance; apertures about one centre are nested/correlated and bins within a profile are not fully independent (channel correlation is in the nulls). Xb4b-vs-Xb4d ratio systematic 5% (measured 0.5-2% core). Wing windows beyond +-150 km/s are noise-limited in at least one line; limits are 2-sigma. Contamination of the HCN wings by CH3NH2/CH3CHO and of HCO+ by CH3OH/CH3CHO is judged from the catalogue only (not quantified); the symmetric blue/red HCN excess at N argues against a one-sided blend. The N/S ladder forward model assumes the Xb4d compact-flux weights and constant per-nucleus R, and has chi2/dof 6-16; Xb4d recovers 78-80% of the Xb4f 3-2 flux. RADEX uses a single zone, equal filling for both lines and 150 km/s FWHM (columns scale as N/dv); results are consequences of each interpretation, not unique solutions. Previous 'flat with velocity'/'no opacity signature' wording is superseded.

Q2: RADEX is a one-zone uniform-sphere model on a 0.25 dex grid; the N fit is marginal in one-zone (see Q12: profile chi2 9.2/4 dof, p~0.05; earlier chi2 19-23/8 are not goodness-of-fit values at best fit), the temperature floor was removed (S Tkin 15-50 K, N 25-100 K), X, n, T and filling are degenerate, N(HCN) per cloud depends on an assumed dv and X(HCN), and the ladder/1-0 data carry a 14%/5% cross-band systematic (Harada 1-0 at 1.7" taken from the paper). Only ranges should be quoted; a two-phase (dense+diffuse) model, HCN IR pumping and chemistry-dependent abundances are not modelled. Disk and outflow regions have no matched multi-J ladders in the data.

Q12c: (a) two-component models have 7-9 effective parameters for 7 data: no chi2 test, AIC/BIC are parameter counting; evidence differences depend on prior volume (n_c cap, filling floor), error floor (14% vs 25%) and geometry priors; (b) geometry widths are measured for the 3-2 emission only (peak Tb at the same position, Gaussian components, 10% scale per OUS, Xb4f recovery f nuisance 0.85+-0.2); 2-1 and 4-3 sizes and the 2-1/4-3 beam matching are assumptions (relative size scatter 0.15-0.30, one 4.47" model beam for all lines); (c) the 1-0 data are literature (Harada+2018, 1.7", 12m only) with a lognormal 0.10 scale nuisance; the N/S blend in the 1-0 beam is unresolved; (d) 12C/13C marginalised 30-100 and a one-sided Gaussian for H13CN with the Q1b/Q4 limit (CO-wing model dependent); (e) lower edge of the T prior is 10 K: the N measured-geometry one-zone T posterior (12-25 K) touches it; (f) LVG sphere only, no slab/IR pumping, Tbg 2.73 K (5 K test; H13CN only at 2.73 K), n_e<n_c; (g) the calibration simulations use the best fit of the truth model, one seed per simulation and 3000 particles; truths T3/T3b are stress tests that are not refit to the data (T3b does not fit them); (h) the deblend variants (16) are not independent draws of the full N-S error; the joint Delta T uses their spread only (floor-only errors per variant); (i) the earlier Q12b numbers (8 data, N T 17-61 K, 'chi2 9.2/4') and the Q4c chi2 19-23/8 are superseded by this statistic; a bug in the u-prior of a first Q12c run (negative chi2) was found and all two-component runs with u priors were rerun.

Q8: (a) the Xb47/Xb4f short-baseline loss is inferred from a model, not measured: the two families (unbounded vs Bmin>=15 m) give corrected HCN N/S 1.18 vs 0.96 and the 50/50 pooling is a judgement; real uv holes are not Gaussian and cleaning partially restores flux; (b) Xb47 and Xb55 are assumed to share Xb4f's configuration/minimum baseline (supported by the beam ratios = wavelength ratios, not by visibilities); (c) 4-3 sizes assumed equal to 3-2 (compact x0.7 tested); (d) the continuum alpha bound (1.5-4.5) and equal-alpha estimate are assumptions; (e) position samples of blended maps (deblended contrast is larger, 1.47 uncorrected, but suffers the same recovery); (f) control-pair null uses 31-59 positions and non-independent pairs, and includes real T43/T32 variations; (g) one-zone RADEX with shared filling; compact-component excitation unconstrained; (h) emcee chains of 40-60k steps (tau 400-1700) are adequate for medians/68% intervals but not for tails.

Q14: all ratios to HCO+ are line (Tb) ratios, not abundances: Tex (factor ~3 per 10 K for CH3OH, x2 for CS 7-6/4-3) and HCO+ opacity (tau32 6-30) are unconstrained; CH3OH N/S/Bridge excitation rests on one Band-6 line and a Band-5 blend with a 30-45% baseline systematic from the spw22 edge ramp (mechanism inferred, no uv data); Xb4d vs Xb4f CH3OH recovery (55-77%) makes the 1" N/S limits valid for compact emission only; N and S are separated by <1.3 beams at 4-6" so the Xb47/Xb4f values are peak-position values including leakage (~10-30%, Q1 deblend); the 252.34 GHz feature is a CH2NH/HC3N blend; SiO, HC3N 10-9, CS 2-1 and SO 219.949 are not covered, so Harada's SiO variation is untested. A second low-Eu CH3OH line at <=4" and a 1-0/2-1 map at ~1" would decide the N-vs-S excitation.

Q14 round 2: (a) the matched Harada test uses a feather correction that assumes Xb4f complete and a smooth deficit; Xb4d/Xb4f array types are inferred from beams, not from visibilities; (b) S-N CH3OH is 2.8-3.0 sigma per array (moderate); both nuclei sit on the slope of Bridge/W-clump emission; (c) RADEX uses p-H2 collisions only and a 150 km/s FWHM, beam filling 1; Tex(254)~5-7 K and N(CH3OH) 1.7-4.9x LTE depend on n=1e5.5-1e6.5 inferred from one ratio at a 9.4x6.3" beam; (d) dust N(H2) assumes kappa, Td 20-50 K and continuum free of line flux; (e) the 29SiO-H2CS blend is 29 km/s apart so 29SiO limits are a factor ~2.3 looser than the H2CS=0 fit; the SiO limits are 5-360x above Harada's SiO/CS, i.e. not a test.

Q13: (a) E significance depends on the noise estimator: 4.4 sigma with the conservative random-aperture null (this work), 6.2 sigma with the smaller field-rms (team-b); (b) Xb4b has too little sensitivity at 1.05" to confirm the excess (expected S/N 1.5-2.5 even at full recovery) and R decreases with aperture, consistent with partly resolved-out extended gas but not required; (c) HDO 266.161 GHz has no companion line in the data: for arbitrary kinematics the blend fraction is unconstrained by the spectrum, constrained only by the chemical argument (>=7-17x lobe-specific enhancement) and the weak 4-3 check; (d) the lobe channels are outside the Xb4d clean masks (uncleaned, dirty-beam flux scale); (e) HCO+ 4-3 unusable at the lobe (baseline), so no E at 4-3; (f) HCN/HCO+ in the lobe is window-dependent (0.6 core, 1.3-1.8 E window, 0.74 whole component), so a single ratio must not be used in RADEX without stating the window. Confirmation needs a second HDO line or HCN/HCO+ 4-3 at <=1" with a clean mask extending to -400 km/s.

Q15: (a) the red-side baseline is an extrapolation (all line-free channels are blue of the line), giving +-40% on the HCN ridge flux and 2-4 sigma on HCO+; (b) significance is pointwise at an a-priori position (team-b p0017, M18) and the red-window noise is non-Gaussian; (c) no CO or low-J HCN/HCO+ at <=1" in the archive, so kinematic discrimination of counter-lobe vs Bridge/N streaming is not possible with ratios (HCN/HCO+ 3.3+-1.8 vs 2.0+-0.7) or the p-v alone; (d) Xb47 4-3 is blended at 4.5" and baseline-limited; (e) fluxes are 1.05" beam aperture values from uncleaned channels (Q13e), i.e. lower limits for extended emission; (f) dynamical times are projected with no inclination correction.

Q5 (round 2): (a) Xb4b recovers ~0.5 of the flux, so sizes are of the compact component; (b) injection calibrates the noise-limited error (0.01-0.06") only: the dominant error is non-Gaussian structure (radius dependence 1.1-12x), so sizes beyond the stable subset are ranges/limits; the null maps are only 2 (HCN) and 1 (HCO+) independent blocks, reused at random positions; (c) the offset budget has no independent astrometric check (one execution, one continuum image, no repeat in Xb4d/Xb4f), so 0.03-0.1" displacements are limits, not detections; (d) the forward model assumes an axisymmetric thin disk with a single Gaussian (or measured-map) intensity, one kinematic axis, no warp/outflow, sigma_int(R) with an exponential form; N fit chi2_red 3.4, S 13.6 (HCN S 69, not used); errors are inflated by the pixel-correlation factor 2.7 but are not full posteriors; the N-S Mdyn ratio of 1.4-5 reflects inclination priors (N 20-40, S 70-90 deg, from Sakamoto+2014) and the poor S fit; (e) the HCN/HCO+ half-light-radius comparison is a model-independent result at 0.30" but depends on the background annulus (0.01-0.03"); (f) clean beam is Gaussianised (the Xb4b PSF has side lobes), which can bias deconvolved sizes <~0.05"; (g) dynamical masses include stars and all gas; virial masses assume virialised gas.

Q22 (round 2): (a) the 10 arcsec ladders are team-b p0028 values, not matched in uv/beam to the 1.7 arcsec data, one flux scale per band per nucleus; (b) the aperture-overlap treatment assumes the other core contributes 0.5x (edge of aperture; 0 and 1 tested) and a single shared uniform envelope; (c) uniform-sphere RADEX zones, one line width, X(HCN) equal in core and envelope; masses scale with the assumed 10 arcsec envelope area and 1/X; (d) P(Te>=50) depends on Tbg (2.73 vs 5 K), the T prior and varies 0.1-0.8 between variants; (e) lnZ seed scatter 0.4-1.1 (2.9 for k=22); profile chi2 is the best of the final SMC particles; (f) the single-state rejection at N rests on the HCN-vs-HCO+ pattern of the 10 arcsec lines and drops to dlnZ~5 if either species is removed; (g) p0041 (team-b) finds the N-S abundance contrast only ~2 sigma and a bimodal N temperature, consistent with the poorly constrained N core temperature here.
